**The power cap on the flown force** (D-SP7-50, KI-045). The force law's power cap
applies to the force that is flown, after the stop taper:

    F = min(F_h + (min(F_lim(t), F_max) - F_h) w(s), P_max/sdot)   (the cap for sdot > 0),   F_h = M g_a - T_sys

so F sdot <= P_max on every branch, the taper's included. `pre_power_force_N` is the
tapered force for the force law (the acceleration law's capped command, its taper in the
command, as before) and `drive_force_N` caps it by P_max/sdot. Where w = 1 (no taper, or
before it) the operations are S4's F = min(F_lim, F_max, P_max/sdot), float for float,
so constant_accel, every acceleration-law push and every force-law push that never enters
a taper are bit-identical (measured on 1-D and fixed-guidance planar runs before and
after the change: their time series, events and every metric value). The `power_limit`
watch reads the flown force: (F_pre sdot - P_max)/F_max with F_pre the tapered force
inside the taper (the margin of P_max/sdot over the force the cap applies to, written as
a product so it stays finite at sdot = 0); the event set and the sub-phase splitting of
S4 are otherwise unchanged. Where the cap binds in the taper the flown force is
P_max/sdot and the motion is the power phase, whatever the taper weight; the cap lets go
where the tapered force falls to P_max/sdot (`power_limit_end`), and from there the
taper's position form holds. S4 applied the taper after the cap, F_h + (min(F_law,
P_max/sdot) - F_h) w, which flew below the rated power in the taper (0.28 % slower exit on
the review's probe) and above P_max/sdot wherever P_max/sdot < F_h.

Closed form (vertical, cold, F_0 = M g, the corner v_c = P/F_max before the taper;
`test_the_power_cap_applies_to_the_tapered_force_in_closed_form`): the power phase of
"Linear motor" (t - t_c and s - s_c with v_inf = P/(M g)) runs into the taper
(`taper_start` at s_0 = L - s_t, v_0 the root of s(v_0) = s_0); the cap lets go at v_1,
the root of (M g + M a_f (L - s(v))/s_t) v = P with a_f = F_max/M - g, s_1 = s(v_1), t_1 =
t(v_1); then x = L - s obeys x'' = -(a_f/s_t) x from x_1 = L - s_1 at v_1: v^2 = v_1^2 +
Omega^2 (x_1^2 - x^2), v_e^2 = v_1^2 + Omega^2 x_1^2, t_e = t_1 + atan(Omega x_1/v_1)/Omega,
Omega = sqrt(a_f/s_t). The cap does not bind again: d/dt [(M g + M a_f x/s_t) v] = M
Omega^2 (2 Omega^2 x^2 + g x - v_1^2 - Omega^2 x_1^2), negative at x_1 (the cap letting
go) and falling further as x falls toward 0 (the bracket increases with x for x > 0, and
x only decreases after x_1).

*Where P_max/sdot < F_h.* On a straight track with a thrust that does not fall (every
track a config builds) this edge is never reached: F_h = M g sin phi - T_sys does not
rise (M falls, T rises or holds), the drive force before the cap is never below F_h
(F_lim >= F_0 >= F_h(0), w in [0, 1]), so sdot cannot pass P_max/F_h(t), where a capped
push stops accelerating. It needs a holding force that rises along the track, which a
curved track gives: `test_the_power_cap_binds_below_the_holding_force_on_an_arc` injects
an arc from horizontal to vertical (R = L/(pi/2)) and a push power-limited from v_c = 10
m/s that carries a speed above P/F_h into a 60 m taper. The flown force there is
P_max/sdot, below F_h (the stack slows); F sdot <= P_max (1 + 1e-12) at every integrator
step and every sampled row, where S4's order would have flown more than 1.001 P_max
(computed in the test); the exit agrees with an independent quadrature of the scalar ODE
M sddot = F - M g sin phi(s) (solve_ivp, DOP853, rtol 1e-12, restarted at the rise end,
the cap binding or letting go and the taper start).

**Release at a target speed** (design 4.7). `LinearMotorConfig.release_speed_mps`
v_release (> 0, strict and finite; left out of the dump when unset; refused together with
any `stop_taper_m`, 0 included: the taper brings the push to its holding force at L, a
release-at-L device, design 4.6) reaches the model as `LinearMotorAssist.release_speed_mps`
(refused with a taper, and when not finite or not > 0) and the protocol's
`release_speed_mps` (None for constant_accel and none). `fly_track` lists the terminal
event `target_speed` (`engine.ev_release_speed`: sdot - v_release crossing upward,
zero_tol ATOL_MPS) in every sub-phase of such a push and flies it to as a fixed end, like
every crossing ("Linear motor", *Second flight*). The exit: a sub-phase that ends at
`target_speed`, or with sdot >= v_release - ATOL_MPS (a crossing at a watch, or a second
flight a hair short: so no sub-phase starts with the event in its zero band), and not at
`track_end`, releases there. Its TrackExit holds z, phi and x at the release position s
(z = start + z(s), phi(s), x = 0 on a vertical StraightTrack and s cos phi otherwise),
`release_position_m` = s and `release_trigger` = `target_speed`; the `target_speed`
event is logged at the release (an ASSIST event, before the planner's `release`); and the
run gains the run-specific assumption line of `early_release_assumption`, worded for the
flight model (`PreludeLayout.aerodynamic`: True for the planar prelude) and the track
(fix round 1): "linear_motor: released at the release speed <v> m/s at s = <s> m, <L - s>
m before the track end (L = <L> m; the track exit at the ground, the silo mouth), at
altitude <z> m: the vehicle flies in the vented shaft after the release <as the model
flies>[; the floor of the flight model in the shaft is the parked carriage at z = <z_f>
m: a fall back onto it, from inside the shaft or through the open mouth, is an impact (no
catch and re-hold)]; the carriage brakes from the release point (facility max(L, s +
braking distance): within the stroke left when s + braking distance <= L, else past the
track end; in place of L + braking distance); the ideal screening estimate is taken at
this release speed, not at the speed at the track exit, which <changes>" (fix round 4,
H4-m4: 'the rest of the vented shaft' and 'brakes in the stroke left' were false for a
fall back and for a carriage that brakes past the mouth; V4-2: the bracketed floor clause
when the floor lies below the ground). The planar model flies it "as in the
open atmosphere at its altitude (no shaft flow model and no walls: drag, dynamic
pressure and Mach number are computed as in open air, and stage 1 may light and its
pitch kick begin there, with no clearance check: the offset at the ground is the
downrange of the shaft_exit event, logged when the kick began in the shaft)", <changes>
being "gravity, drag and any thrust over the rest of the track change (the gravity and
drag over it are in the flight's losses, the thrust in its delta-v)"; the 1-D model "as
the 1-D flight flies everywhere: drag-free, with vacuum thrust (no atmosphere; no shaft
flow model, no walls)" ("with the thrust at the constant ambient pressure <p> Pa" for a
planner built with p_amb > 0, which no experiment builds: `sim.simulate` builds every
1-D planner at 0 Pa) and "gravity and any thrust over the rest of the track change (the
gravity over it is in the flight's losses, the thrust in its delta-v)" (fix round 2,
H2-m2: thrust is not a loss, and the 1-D model has no atmosphere and no kick). The exit is called the silo mouth only when it is at the ground
(within ATOL_M); a release above the ground (a tower exit) flies "over the rest of the
track's length", and one below a tower exit "in the vented shaft and on the track above
the ground after the release". A push that reaches the track end below
v_release - ATOL_MPS releases there (`track_end`) with the flag
`release_speed_not_reached: the push reached <v_L> m/s at the track end (s = L = <L> m),
below the release speed <v> m/s; it released at the track end`; its push is bit for bit
that of the same drive without a release speed (an event that never fires moves no
step). A `track_end` exit keeps z(L), phi(L) and x of SP1 bit for bit (the same
expressions). TrackExit's two new fields have defaults: it is not reached by the 1-D
golden dump (D-SP7-27; `tests/test_golden_dump_fields.py` lists what is). The metrics
read the release from the trace (`metrics.release_point`): the `target_speed` ASSIST
event marks the trigger and s is the last ASSIST phase's end state (the release state);
otherwise L and `track_end`.

The release maps take the release altitude: the 1-D `map_release` (vertical, z at s)
and the planar `map_release_planar` (a vertical exit with x = 0, unchanged; r = r_datum +
z(s)). The planar track's constant ambient pressure stays p(z at L). A height-event
ignition (`height_method: event`; on this drive only an injected spec, as the config
converts no ramp start for it) lights at the mouth plus h, not at the release point plus
h, in both planners (z(L) + h: the same float as before for a release at L).

Closed forms of the release position the tests use (cold, vertical, M constant, g =
g_eff): the acceleration law on its plateau, v^2 = 2 a s - a^2 t_r^2/12, so s_rel =
(v_release^2 + a^2 t_r^2/12)/(2 a) at t = t_r/2 + v_release/a; the force law on its force
phase, s_rel = s_r + (v_release^2 - v_r^2)/(2 a_f) at t = t_r + (v_release - v_r)/a_f (v_r
= a_f t_r/2 and s_r = a_f t_r^2/6 at the end of the rise from F_0 = M g), and on its power
phase s_rel = s_c + s(v_release) at t_c + t(v_release) (the power phase from v_c, "Linear
motor"); a release speed at a kink of the drive, the end of the rise (v_r at t_r) or the
power corner (v_c, where `power_limit`'s value sdot - P/F_max and `target_speed`'s share
their root), releases there.

**After a release below the mouth.** The vehicle begins its free flight inside the vented
shaft (z < 0 for a buried silo). The 1-D planner lists the impact in falling phases only,
so nothing changes there while it rises. The planar planner lists the ground event in
every burn sub-phase (`_burn`: the vertical rise after an apex, the kick, the gravity
turn), whose already-past rule would end a burn starting below the ground at once as an
impact. So a burn sub-phase that starts more than ATOL_M below the ground altitude while
rising (`PlanarPlanner._in_shaft` and `_rising`) lists instead `shaft_exit` (the altitude
crossing the ground upward, `ev_altitude_up`) and `shaft_apex` (the radial apex), each of
which ends the sub-phase only (and is logged, as every planar event is): from the mouth
on the ground is armed as on every other flight. `shaft_exit` is therefore logged only
when a burn sub-phase that lists the ground (KICK, GRAVITY_TURN, the rise after an apex)
is in flight at the mouth crossing, that is, whenever the kick has begun inside the
shaft; a vehicle that leaves the shaft in the pre-ignition coast or in the vertical rise
(sub-phases that list no ground event while rising) logs no crossing: it is not steered
off the vertical before its kick (fix round 1, P1-m5). Its downrange there is the
vehicle's offset from the shaft axis at the mouth; no clearance against the shaft wall
is checked (the model has no walls), and the replay's close-up note reports it (to the
page's 1 m). On a powered sub-phase whose apex has a downward acceleration below
APEX_FOLD_ACCEL_MPS2 a crossing just below that apex can go unlogged ("Event rules",
`ev_altitude_up`); the apex then ends the sub-phase above the mouth and the flight is
unchanged. A vehicle that stops rising inside the shaft (an apex below the ground) falls
back: its next sub-phase starts below the ground falling, where the ground's impact event
is already past. In its place the falling sub-phase lists the impact at the floor of the
shaft, the parked carriage (fix round 3, P3-M1): z_floor = z(s_release) + d_brake sin
phi(s_release) (`prelude.shaft_floor_m`, from the TrackExit and the carriage's braking
distance at the release speed; `metrics.carriage_park_altitude_m` of the same run),
carried by the 1-D `ascend`'s `floor_m` and the planar `FlightStart.shaft_floor_m` into
every coast and burn (`_shaft_floor_for` in both planners). A carriage braking at a total
deceleration a_b no smaller than the vehicle's (g_eff, plus the drag, less any thrust)
stays below the vehicle and is parked by v/a_b, before the vehicle, past its apex at v/g
or later, can come back down, so the parked carriage is the first obstacle of the fall;
the model has no contact with the carriage on its braking path or with the shaft walls.
A falling burn lists the turnaround as every falling burn does (1-D: `turnaround`; the
planar vertical rise: its `turnaround` split; KICK, GRAVITY_TURN and the other planar
burns: `SHAFT_TURNAROUND_EVENT`, which ends the sub-phase only), so the thrust turns the
vehicle around above the carriage as it does above the ground; the burns and the coasts
list the floor's impact in place of the ground's. Released at 10 m/s about 98 m down and
lit 0.5 s later on the F9's 2 s ramp, the 1-D vehicle turns around at -93.540 m, 3.43 m
above its carriage, and flies to burnout, within 1e-3 m of the same push on a track moved
up out of the ground (mu/r^2 differs by about 3e-5 between the two release radii); the
planar flight turns around at -96.506 m (carriage at -96.974 m) and kicks at 198 m, 0.04
m and 0.75 m from its moved-up twin (its back pressure is higher at 100 m less altitude,
and mu/r^2 and omega_p differ; the F9 of these tests, generic_f9_class.yaml, has no aero
block, so no drag enters: fix round 5, P5-m2). Before S4a fix round 3 both planners ended such a run at once at
the apex (P3-M1: a recoverable flight read as an impact).

*Over the shaft* (fix round 4, P4-M1). A vehicle released below the mouth whose apex lies
above the mouth falls back through the open mouth, not onto the ground: the mouth is an
opening, and its first obstacle is the carriage below it. So when the floor lies more than
ATOL_M below the ground, a falling sub-phase over the shaft lists the floor's impact in
place of the ground's whether it starts above or below the mouth (`_shaft_floor_for`),
and a start on the ground is then no impact at t0. Over the shaft means every 1-D
sub-phase (the 1-D flight never leaves the shaft's axis) and, planar, the sub-phases
before the kick (`over_shaft`: the pre-ignition coast, the vertical rise and a failed
stage 1's terminal coast, which never kicks; the Coriolis drift before the kick is
centimetres); after the kick, and after a vertical-only rise's MECO, the ground stays the
surface of a sub-phase that starts above it. A floor at or above the ground (a release
at the mouth, whose carriage parks d_brake above it, or a carriage braking past the
mouth) keeps the obstacle-free fall to the ground of Phase 1 ("Failed-ignition coast").
Before fix round 4 the floor stopped at the mouth, so the outcome jumped at apex = mouth:
on the F9 (a = 3 g0, a 5 g0 brake, lit 4 s after the release) 38.0 m/s turned around at
-16.257 m (twin -16.250) and flew on, while 38.5 and 39 m/s (apex 1.1 m and 3.8 m above
the mouth) hit the ground at z = 0 at 4.2 and 6.2 m/s. Now 38.5 m/s turns around at
-12.120 m (twin -12.112 m) and 39 m/s at -8.019 m (twin -8.012 m), 47 and 50 m above
their carriages; planar (`to_kick`, the 28.5 deg site, on the drag-free F9:
generic_f9_class.yaml has no aero block) 38.5, 39 and 40 m/s kick at 234 to 249 m, 0.5 m
from their twins, where they raised GuidanceFailure "hit the ground at t = 6.03 s before
the kick". A failed ignition released at 50 m/s rises 70 m above the mouth and falls back
onto its carriage 31.7 m below the mouth at 44.73 m/s (the energy speed), where it hit the
ground at 37.1 m/s with the carriage items None. On the drag-carrying
generic_f9_class_2d.yaml the same failed ignition lands on its carriage at 44.7121 m/s,
0.029 m/s below the drag-free 44.7411 m/s, 9.6916 s after the release, matching an
independent radial quadrature with the vehicle's drag, mu/r^2 and omega_p^2 r (Coriolis
neglected) to 1e-8 m/s and 1.5e-6 s (fix round 5, P5-m2:
`test_a_planar_fall_back_with_drag_matches_a_radial_quadrature`).

A fall onto the carriage ends the run in an impact there, at the event root, however slow
the touchdown (no catch and re-hold is modelled: on the pad the same vehicle would be
held until its thrust exceeds its weight; touchdowns at 0.6 to 2.2 m/s on the carriage end
lit 1-D runs released at 4 to 20 m/s; a KI candidate), and `_flag_floor_impact` adds the
plain run flag "<kind> at t = <t> s: shaft_fallback: the vehicle fell back inside the
shaft, after a release below the ground, onto the parked carriage at z = <z> m (<d> m
below the ground) at <v> m/s: the impact is logged there (the model's floor in the shaft
is the carriage, parked after braking from the release; any touchdown on it ends the
run, no catch and re-hold being modelled; no contact with the shaft walls)", <v> the
touchdown speed (|v| in 1-D, the Earth-relative |v_rel| in planar; fix round 4, P4-m2).
The floor applies to any release below the ground, a constant_accel push to a buried
track exit included (TrackConfig allows exit_altitude_m < 0; no shipped experiment has
one): a 1 g0 push of 20 m to an exit 50 m down with a failed ignition now ends on its
carriage at -46.0 m at 17.7 m/s, where before S4a fix round 3 the engine's already-past
rule ended it at once at its apex, -29.98 m, with an opaque note (fix round 4, P4-m1,
C4-m2). A falling
sub-phase that starts within ATOL_M above the floor or below it (`_at_floor`: a carriage
braking at less than the vehicle's deceleration parks above the apex, its braking path
meeting the vehicle where the model has no contact), or with no floor known (a flight
started below the ground without a track release, which only a test builds), is an
impact at once at that apex (`_shaft_fallback`, the zero-length pass-through of fix round
1), its flag "... the vehicle stopped rising <d> m below the ground (z = <z> m), inside
the shaft after a release below the ground, at or below the parked carriage's altitude z
= <z_f> m (braking at less than the vehicle's deceleration, the carriage met it on its
braking path, where the model has no contact) | with no shaft floor known (no track
release): the impact is logged at once at that apex". Which record carries it (fix round
2, P2-M2): the 1-D run and the planar failed-ignition coast keep that trace, so the note
is a run flag; on the planar flight every experiment runs, the impact ends `to_kick` (or
`from_kick`, or the staging coast) in a GuidanceFailure whose trace is discarded, so
`PlanarPlanner._impact_failure` words the failure from the same note with `logged`
False (fix round 3, H3-m2: nothing is recorded): "impact: the vehicle's flight ended
inside the shaft at t = <t> s before the kick: shaft_fallback: the vehicle fell back
inside the shaft, after a release below the ground, onto the parked carriage at z = <z> m
(<d> m below the ground) at <v> m/s: the run ends in an impact there (the failed trace is
not kept, so no event is recorded) (...)" (the run's one `guidance_failed` flag; "the
vehicle's flight ended" since fix round 4, H4-m2, as an apex impact does not fall; the
touchdown speed since P4-m2; "hit the ground" stays the wording of an impact at the
ground). Such a run has an empty time series, so the replay and the scene
leave it out, and the summary's linear-motor rows read n/a for it. The impact is thus
logged inside the shaft (on the carriage, or at the apex), not where the base returns to
the ground; the scene's drawn impact note, which says the latter, is corrected by the
scene's caveat and, on every captured frame, by its fall-back frame line (fix round 3,
H3-m1) for such a run, worded by where the impact is (fix round 5, M1, P5-M1): on the
carriage, both the note's "no contact with the carriage" and its "altitude 0" are
corrected; at the apex, where the vehicle stopped rising and the model had no contact
with the carriage parked above it, only its "altitude 0". Both are keyed on the run's
`shaft_fallback` flag, not on its release trigger, so a release at a buried track exit
gets them too (fix round 5, M2). Every sub-phase of a flight that starts at or above the ground lists the
events of SP2, in their order (the bit-identity check above included the planar pad and
silo runs), and no falling sub-phase of such a flight starts below the ground or lists
a floor (its floor, where it has one, lies at or above the ground). The carriage brakes
from the release point: facility = max(L, s_release + d_brake), within the stroke left
when s_release + d_brake <= L, else past the track end
(`LinearMotorAssist.facility_length_m(track, v, s_release)`, written into
`facility_length_m` by `metrics.linear_motor_facility_m`; L + d_brake to the bit for a
release at L), and the 1-D failed-ignition carriage parks at z(s_release) + d_brake sin
phi(s_release) (`carriage_park_altitude_m`). The braking metrics use the speed at release;
`push_accel_mean_mps2` = v_exit/t_push stays a mean.

**Metrics** (KI-052; LINEAR_MOTOR_METRICS, 18 keys): `push_control_law` (`force` or
`acceleration`), `push_accel_command_mps2` (a_cmd; None for the force law),
`push_stop_taper_m` (None without a taper) and `push_release_speed_mps` (None when no
release speed is set; a push that does not reach it keeps the set value, with
`release_trigger` `track_end` and the flag) join the settings of S4, for a linear-motor
run only (no field of a dataclass the 1-D golden dump reaches); `release_position_m` and
`release_trigger` read the real release. Fix round 1 adds `push_cap_bound`
(`metrics._cap_bound`: under the acceleration law a `drive_cap` event before the
release, with `_power_limited`'s tie; False: no cap bound, so the push flew its command
wherever it ran; True: a cap bound at some time, which the key does not record (fix
round 2: on the 1-D F9 at a_cmd 3 g0 and t_r 0.5 s a cap at F_max = 0.9 M (a + g) binds
at 0.433 s, inside the rise, and never lets go, and one at 0.85 M (a + g) on a hot push
binds at 0.459 s and lets go at 0.772 s); None for the force law and for a stalled
push), so the readers can say whether an acceleration-law push held its command (with
its release time against t_r: `replay.motor_acceleration_text`).

**The readers.** No single push acceleration is claimed for a drive that does not hold
one, a plateau the drive does hold is not denied, a mean is named a mean, and a release
before the mouth is stated (fix round 1 reworded S4a's first readers, which said every
linear-motor push "holds no constant acceleration": false for an acceleration-law push
with no binding cap, which holds a_cmd after its rise, and for the plateau of a cold
force-law push at F_max).

- app.py: its run browser and results panel read a linear-motor directory through

**Assumption lines.** With a release speed, `release_assumption` replaces the release
line: "linear_motor: release where the speed along the track reaches the release speed <v>
m/s (assumed), before the track end, or at the track end (s = L) when the push does not
reach it there (flag release_speed_not_reached); no stop taper: the drive force drops to
zero in a step at release, and the carriage brakes from the release (facility max(L,
s_release + braking distance): within the stroke left, or past the track end when the
braking distance exceeds it)" (fix round 4, H4-m4's sibling: "in the stroke left beyond
the release" was false past the mouth); the shaft line then says that the air drag on the
vehicle in the shaft is neglected during the push (after a release before the track end
the flight model flies on in the shaft after it, as the early-release line says)
and what it would do to where the push reaches that speed (under the force law it would
delay the release, the release position and the push time biased low, the speed at
release the release speed while the push still reaches it and biased high when it
releases at the track end without reaching it; under the acceleration law, while no cap
binds, the release position is unchanged, and while a cap binds the release is delayed,
or the speed at a release at the track end biased high). The force law's taper line
names the cap's order: "the force limit is scaled toward the holding force ... by min(1,
(L - s) / s_taper), and the power cap P_max / sdot applies to the scaled force
(D-SP7-50); at L the drive force is the holding force ... (zero net acceleration) unless
the power cap binds there (never on a straight track a config builds)".

**Measured** (scratch probes, not run by the suite; relative to L, v_e and t_e at rtol
1e-12, 1e-11 and 1e-10): the power cap in the taper, the exit 6.3e-16 to 8.5e-16, its
power_limit_end 3.3e-15 to 3.7e-15, every step 5e-15 or better; the arc against its
quadrature 2.2e-15 to 6.0e-15 in speed and 1.4e-13 to 2.4e-13 in time; the plateau
release 1.2e-16 (speed) and 2.1e-16 (s); the force and power phases 1.7e-15 or better;
the release at the end of the rise 2.4e-16; at the power corner 1.4e-16 to 2.8e-16 at
rtol 1e-12 and 1e-10 and 5e-12 at rtol 1e-11, where the push released by the ATOL_MPS tie
at the end of a flight that stopped a hair before the root (up to ATOL_MPS/v early: 2e-11
relative at 50 m/s). The tests assert 1e-9: margins above 1e5, and 200 at the tie.

**Stays out of S4a:** a shaft flow model after an early release; a clearance check of
the vehicle against the shaft wall after a kick that begins in the shaft (the offset at
the mouth is reported, not checked); the scene's carriage braking from s_release (the
frozen template; stated in the scene's caveat and frame caveat instead); a `target_speed`
crossing passed over inside one integrator step (sdot is monotone on every vented push a
config builds: the drive force is never below the holding force before a cap and the cap
never below it on a straight track; the scan of *Passed over* reads the two-way watches
only; a sealed push's sdot is not monotone (S5), and there a release speed up to 2e-5
m/s below its speed peak was passed over on the pushes measured, the push releasing at L
with a `release_speed_not_reached` flag that misstates it: "The sealed shaft", Speed
along the stroke); the structural transform on a flown push (S4b, done: "The flown push
of a linear motor").

## The sealed shaft (SP7 step S5)

Modules: `assist/linear_motor.py` (`SealedShaft`, `ShaftKind`, `SHAFT_SEALED`,
`WORK_STATE`, `SEALED_TAPER_REFUSAL`; `LinearMotorAssist.shaft`, `extra_state_names`,
`piston_force_N`, `command_force_N`, `state_rate`, `at_push_start` with
`PushStart.column_end_N`, `stall_reason`, `control_assumption`, `taper_assumption`,
`shaft_assumption`, `sealed_assumptions`), `atmosphere.py` (`KAPPA_AIR`), `config.py`
(`ShaftKind`, `SHAFT_SEALED`, `SEALED_SHAFT_KEYS`, `LinearMotorConfig`'s shaft keys,
`body_diameter_m`, `_check_sealed_bore` in `resolve_run`), `losses.py` (`PistonWork`,
`piston_work`, `assist_identity_residual_rel`), `metrics.py` (`SEALED_SHAFT_METRICS`,
`sealed_shaft_piston`, `sealed_shaft_metrics`, `track_metrics`), `metrics_planar.py`
(`planar_track_metrics`), `summary.py` (`SEALED_SHAFT_ROWS`). Tests:
`tests/test_sealed_shaft.py`; two in `tests/test_structure_linear_motor.py`; the pins of
`tests/vented_pins_support.py` (`tests/data/vented_pins.json`). Design 4.8, D-SP7-26,
D-SP7-27, the S5 row of section 5; docs/phases/inputs/2026-10-08-SP7-sources.md section
10 (`shaft_bore_m` 3.7, `shaft_gap_m` 5.0 (1.0 to 20.0), `shaft_gamma` 1.4, all assumed
but gamma, the ICAO adiabatic index); surveys 01 (sections 6, 7.5 and 9), 07 (section 9)
and 08 (A3).

**Config.** `shaft: vented | sealed` on `linear_motor` (`ShaftKind`; vented the default,
so every vented block validates and dumps as before). `sealed` needs `shaft_bore_m` d (>
0), `shaft_gap_m` h_0 (> 0) and `shaft_gamma` gamma (> 1, the work's closed form divides
by gamma - 1), strict and finite (KI-030's rule); the three are refused with `vented`
(given at all, a null included) and left out of the dump while None. `resolve_run`, where
the run and its vehicle meet, refuses a bore at or below the diameter d = sqrt(4
A_ref/pi) of the run's A_ref (`body_diameter_m`, which the check calls: the vehicle's
aero block after the run's overrides, the main-body section in the vehicle files or the
section an override sets; 3.6598 m for A_ref = 10.52 m^2: the 3.7 m bore passes, and so
does 3.66 m, the nominal body that A_ref's source rounds, since the check uses the
diameter derived from A_ref as given), and a sealed shaft on a vehicle without an aero
block (no diameter to check against; the 1-D generic F9 has none). The message names
that section, never "the body diameter" of a fairing's area. A sealed shaft with the
force law's stop taper (> 0 m) is refused by the config and the model: that taper scales
the force toward the open shaft's holding value M g sin phi - (1 - f_imp) T, so at L the
column would decelerate the stack by F_p(L)/M instead of holding it, and a slow stack
could stop in the shaft; the acceleration law's taper flies its command, the column
included, and is accepted. constant_accel keeps `shaft: Literal["vented"]` and its line
(D-SP7-26: the sealed shaft on `linear_motor` only).

**The bore and the vehicle's largest section** (reported plainly, since it undercuts the
sealed variant's geometry). The check sees the run's A_ref section only (the main body in
the vehicle files), not the vehicle's largest section. The F9 class's fairing is 5.2 m
across and 13.1 m tall on a 70 m stack (configs/display/f9_class.yaml, sourced to the
spacex.com Falcon 9 page; display-only geometry, which the model does not read): in a
100 m silo it starts 30.0 to 43.1 m below the mouth, inside the bore, and would not pass
the 3.7 m bore of sources section 10 (the README's first-order row). A bore that clears
it has more than (5.2/3.7)^2 = 1.975 times the area (3.58 times for the 7.0 m shaft the
scene draws), and p_0 A and W_p scale with the area at a fixed gap. At p_0 =
p_atm(-100 m) and a 5 m gap (scratch probe):

| Bore | p_0 A | F_p(L) | W_p(L) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3.7 m (pre-registered) | 1.10 MN | 1.087 MN | 100.5 MJ |
| 5.2 m (equal to the fairing: the lower limit; refused by the code's own rule for a body) | 2.18 MN | 2.147 MN | 198.6 MJ |
| 7.0 m (the shaft the scene draws) | 3.95 MN | 3.890 MN | 359.9 MJ |

The interface-force drop and the exit-speed loss grow with them, and the choking
argument of the vented alternative changes (a 7.0 m bore around the 5.2 m fairing leaves
(7.0^2 - 5.2^2)/7.0^2 = 45% of the bore open, above the 37.8% Kantrowitz minimum). The
30 m pushes of the S4b tests keep the fairing above the mouth (the stack top at +40 m),
where the body is the right check. The code keeps the pre-registered 3.7 m and states
the gap in the run's lines; which bore lm_fixed_sealed (S6b) flies, or a check against a
stated largest diameter, is the user's decision before S6b. The check already bites in
the project's drag bound: an arm that sets A_ref to the fairing's section, such as
`aero_bound` of experiments/silo_screening_2d.yaml (21.24 m^2, d = 5.20035 m), makes the
check see that section, so a sealed variant with a bore at or below 5.2 m cannot be in
its `of`: `resolve_experiment` then refuses the whole experiment (review probe; the
refusal is physically right, since such a bore does not pass the fairing).

**The column.** The carriage seals the bore above a gap h_0 of air trapped at the
push-start pressure p_0 = p_atm(z_start): the ICAO standard atmosphere at the track
start's altitude (`LinearMotorAssist.from_config`; 102,532 Pa at -100 m, a 100 m silo
whose mouth is at the ground), whatever the flight model's atmosphere (the 1-D model has
none). It is read through `atmosphere.standard_atmosphere`, never through the clamp of
the right-hand side's `ambient_scalar` (review pass 3, C3-m1): a sealed track whose start
exit_altitude_m - L sin phi lies below the ICAO floor `ALT_AMBIANCE_MIN_M` (-5,004 m),
where p_0 is not defined, is refused by the config with a one-line reason, and the model
raises there too. As the carriage rises s along the track the column expands adiabatically,
uniformly and quasi-statically (the push ramps over about 2.6 s against a 0.29 s
acoustic transit of 100 m, survey 07 section 9.2; that transit is the ambient air's, and
the premise weakens near the end of a small-gap stroke, where the gas has cooled to 35
to 110 K and its sound speed, 118 to 211 m/s, is only 1.5 to 3 times the carriage's
76.7 m/s in survey 08's case: the run's not-modelled line, "Assumption lines"):

    p(s)   = p_0 (h_0/(h_0 + s))^gamma
    F_p(s) = max(0, p_0 - p(s)) A,          A = pi d^2/4,     0 <= F_p < p_0 A
    W_p(s) = integral_0^s F_p ds' = p_0 A s - p_0 V_0 [1 - (V_0/V)^(gamma - 1)]/(gamma - 1)

with V_0 = A h_0 and V = A (h_0 + s) (integral_0^s p ds' = p_0 h_0^gamma [(h_0 +
s)^(1 - gamma) - h_0^(1 - gamma)]/(1 - gamma) = p_0 h_0 [1 - (h_0/(h_0 + s))^(gamma -
1)]/(gamma - 1)). Above the carriage the vehicle sits in the shaft open at the mouth, held
at p_0: the open shaft's own hydrostatic drop over the stroke, rho g s sin phi, is left
out with the rest of the air above (about 1.2 kPa over 100 m, 1.2% of p_0), so F_p is
biased high by up to rho g L sin phi A (13 kN, 1.2% of F_p(L), for the 3.7 m bore and the
5 m gap). F_p is the net pressure force on the carriage deck, the open side less the
column, against the motion. Since p > 0, F_p < p_0 A whatever the gas does: 1.0895 MN at
sea level for the 3.7 m bore (the README's 1.1 MN), 1.1024 MN at p_0 = p_atm(-100 m); at
L = 100 m the 5 m gap's column pulls 1.0869 MN, 98.6% of its bound (1.088, 1.074 and
1.001 MN at sea level for 1, 5 and 20 m gaps: survey 07). The code writes F_p = -p_0 A
expm1(-gamma log1p(s/h_0)) and W_p through the same functions, so F_p keeps its digits at
s << h_0; W_p's difference cancels to s/h_0 relative there (its absolute error stays
below 1e-15 p_0 A s). F_p = W_p = 0 at and below s = 0 (the column is never compressed;
a push from rest never goes there).

**Where it acts.** On the carriage, which seals the bore: F_other of the track equation
(`state_rate`),

    M sddot = F + T_sys - M g sin phi - F_p(s),        F_int = m_v (sddot + g sin phi) - T

so the vehicle's free body is unchanged (m_v sddot = F_int + T - m_v g sin phi) and the
carriage's reads m_c sddot = F - F_int - f_imp T - m_c g sin phi - F_p. Hence:

- force law: the drive's force is its law's (min(F_lim(t), F_max, P_max/sdot); F_0 is
  unchanged since F_p(0) = 0); the stack slows, and F_int = [m_v (F - F_p) - T (m_c +
  f_imp m_v)]/M is lower than the vented push's at the same state by (m_v/M) F_p (survey
  01 section 9), the felt g by F_p/(M g0). On a cold push's F_max plateau the felt g
  falls as F_p grows (3.806 g0 at t_r to 3.660 g0 at the release on a 20 t carriage
  with no power phase, against 3.857 g0 held vented; scratch probe), so
  `push_felt_g_plateau`, the felt g at the end of the rise, is the plateau's largest,
  not a value held on it. Released at the track end, the exit speed is lower on every
  push S5's tests and probes measured. With a release speed the speed at release is
  that speed in both shafts while the push reaches it before L (below it, flag
  `release_speed_not_reached`, when the push reaches L first), and the sealed stack
  reaches it later along the track: the release position and the push time are larger
  on every push measured ("Measured"). Both are measured results, not properties of the
  model: the force law's rise r(t), a hot push's T(t) and the falling M(t) give the
  slower sealed stack more force per metre;
- acceleration law: the command F = M (a(t) w(s) + g sin phi) - T_sys + F_p(s) (the
  drive supplies the column too: while no cap binds its force and power rise by F_p and
  F_p sdot, and while no cap binds on the whole push its work rises by W_p and the
  electricity by W_p/eta), then capped as S4 caps it (F_max, P_max/sdot); while no cap
  binds F_int is unchanged; where the vented command already reaches the cap both sit at
  it, the drive force is the same and the stack slows as under the force law, F_int
  lower by (m_v/M) F_p; between the two (the vented command below the cap, the sealed
  one above it) the drive force is the cap and F_int is lower than the vented push's by
  less than (m_v/M) F_p; the `drive_cap` and `power_limit` watches read the command with
  F_p;
- had it acted on the vehicle, F_int would rise by (m_c/M) F_p and the felt-g observable
  would be wrong by F_p/m_v (survey 01 section 9); it does not.

The structural transform (S4b, "The flown push of a linear motor") reads n and F_int from
the flown push through `sim.flown_push_trace` and `sim.linear_motor_push_load`, so the
column's lower F_int and n reach the sizing with no new branch. The push-time estimate
(the step cap and the watch look-ahead only) leaves the column out; it stays exact for
the uncapped acceleration law, which flies its command.

**Push only.** F_p acts from push start to the release, whichever trigger (the track end
or the release speed). After the release the trapped column is not modelled: the carriage
brakes by its own closed form, with no column force on it, and the vehicle above it is
flown as the vented shaft's flight model flies it (the planar model in the open
atmosphere at its altitude, no walls). After a release at the track end the vehicle's
base is at the mouth and sees the shaft open there. After a release before the track end
(a release speed) the braking carriage still seals the bore below the departing vehicle
(review pass 3, P3-m2): the cavity that opens between the vehicle's base and the carriage
deck is closed below and fills only from above, through the bore-body annulus (0.231 m^2,
2.15% of a 3.7 m bore around a 3.66 m body). Left out, each with its direction: a suction
on the vehicle's base section A_body of up to about p_0 A_body (inferred: the vehicle's
speed in the shaft after the release is biased high), and the exhaust of a stage lit
before its base clears the mouth, trapped in that cavity (inferred: the other way). A
review probe (an isothermal cavity with orifice or choked inflow from the open shaft, the
vehicle unlit: an order of magnitude, not a model) for the smoke's release at 60 m/s at s
= 64.75 m, 35.25 m below the mouth: the inflow chokes about 0.1 s after the release, the
suction peaks at about 0.73 MN against p_0 A_body = 1.07 MN (about ten times the 77 kN of
the air pushed out of the mouth, "Assumption lines"), and the vehicle reaches the mouth
0.52 m/s slower (53.42 against 53.93 m/s, after 0.62 s); a stage lit 0.5 s after that
release would light with its base about 6 m inside the bore. A bore that clears the 5.2 m
fairing ("The bore and the vehicle's largest section") leaves a much wider annulus around
the 3.66 m body, and the effect shrinks; a release at the track end and the vented shaft
have neither effect. What the column after the release leaves out, with its direction:
the column pulls the carriage back with up to p_0 A (1.10 MN for the 3.7 m bore at
p_atm(-100 m)), more than a 5 g0 brake's own m_c (a_b - g) = 0.78 MN on a 20 t carriage,
so the brake force, the brake energy and the facility length max(L, s_release + v^2/(2
a_b)) of a sealed run are upper bounds; on a massless carriage (lm_fixed's) the column
has no mass to act on; and a stopped carriage is pulled back down by about p_0 A + m_c g,
which the brake would have to hold. The planar track-push line every planar run carries
("no air drag in the vented shaft") and the early-release line ("in the vented shaft
after the release") keep their vented wording byte for byte; a sealed run's shaft line
reads them as the shaft open above the carriage, where the vehicle flies (S5 changes no
line that a vented run prints).

**Stall against the column.** `at_push_start` binds F_p(L), the column's force at the
track end, its largest on the stroke (`PushStart.column_end_N`, 0 vented), and
`stall_reason` gains a sealed rule after S4's: F_max + (1 - f_imp) T(0) <= M_0 g sin
phi(0) + F_p(L) ends the run at push start with status `drive_stall`, a flag of its own
(the numbers, F_p(L) and the bound p_0 A) and nothing moved (the felt g and
interface-force metrics None, as for S4's stall). It is a conservative guard for every
push. Beyond the point where F_p(s) = F_max + T_sys - M g sin phi the column outweighs the
drive and the thrust, and the speed falls from its peak there. A cold step push (the power
cap never reached; M constant: (1/2) M v^2 = (F_max - M g sin phi) s - W_p(s)) stops
before L, and swings about that point, only when (F_max - M g sin phi) L <= W_p(L); with
F_max - M g sin phi between W_p(L)/L and F_p(L) it would still reach L, slowly, on its
momentum, and the rule refuses it too (0.912 to 0.986 p_0 A, or 92.5% to 100% of F_p(L),
for the 5 m gap over 100 m). The flag says what the rule does not credit: the stack's
momentum, a rising thrust and a falling mass, and with a release speed a release at that
speed before the track end, where the column is below F_p(L) (review pass 3, P3H-m2; a
review probe, rerun: F_max - M g = 0.95 F_p(L), a cold step push with a 3 m/s release
speed, is refused, and with the guard removed it releases at s = 3.61 m at 3.000 m/s,
where flying on it would have peaked at 4.44 m/s at the balance point, 30.87 m). Measured
with the guard removed (scratch
probe: the F9 in 1-D, the test shaft, a cold step push): F_max - M g = 0.97, 0.95 and 0.93
F_p(L) release at L at 4.2453, 3.1637 and 1.4129 m/s, on the energy closed form to 1e-12,
and then fall back; 0.5 F_p(L) stops in the shaft and swings, no event of the push ends
that motion, and the run reaches the integrator's t_max_s = 3600 s and the planner's
RuntimeError. So the guard is needed, and it is conservative. Above it no push stops in
the shaft: under the force law F_max beats the weight and the column on the whole stroke
after the rise and P_max/sdot grows as the speed falls; the acceleration law's capped
force does the same; the force law's taper, which would end toward the open shaft's
holding force, is refused (Config).

**Speed along the stroke** (review pass 3, P3-m1). The guard keeps the speed rising on
the F_max plateau, but a sealed push's speed is not monotone in general: it falls
wherever the drive's force and the thrust's share fall below the weight and the column,
F + T_sys < M g sin phi + F_p(s). The guard prevents a stop, not a fall. Two cases,
measured (scratch probes and a review probe, rerun; the F9 in 1-D, cold, no carriage, the
100 m silo unless stated):

- the power phase, under either law once its power cap binds (the force P_max/sdot is
  the same; measured under the force law): the terminal speed P_max/(M g sin phi +
  F_p(s) - T_sys) falls as the column grows, and a stack that reaches it slows. With
  F_max = m0 (3 g0 + g) and power corners P_max/F_max of 2, 3 and
  4 m/s (5 and 20 m gaps), and of 2 to 6 m/s on a 300 m track, the speed peaks inside the
  track. At a 2 m/s corner it peaks at 6.8417 m/s at s = 12.0 m, where P_max/sdot = M g +
  F_p(s) (to 1.1e-9), against 6.6472 m/s at the exit; at 4 m/s, 13.3104 m/s at 71.7 m
  against 13.2997 m/s. The vented push's terminal speed P_max/(M g sin phi - T_sys) does
  not fall, and its speed stays monotone (0 falling steps at corners of 6 to 15 m/s);
- a slow force rise against a gap far below the sources' 1 to 20 m: the column's
  stiffness p_0 A gamma/h_0 against the slowly rising force makes the stack oscillate on
  it. With F_max = m0 (g0 + g) and t_r = 20 s, gaps of 0.05 and 0.1 m slowed the stack to
  5 and 18 mm/s before it rose again (it stayed positive); gaps of 0.5 m and more, and
  t_r = 4 s, did not.

A release speed below such a peak is met only if the `target_speed` event sees the
upward crossing, and scipy tests its sign only at step ends: an upward crossing in one
step with the peak is passed over (S4a's premise of a monotone sdot holds for the
vented shaft only: "Linear motor", Stays out of S4a). Measured on the test push of the
2 m/s corner (`fly_track`, rtol 1e-11): release speeds 1e-3 to 5e-5 m/s below the peak
release there (trigger `target_speed`); 2e-5 to 1e-9 m/s below it are passed over, and
the push releases at L at 6.6472 m/s with the flag `release_speed_not_reached` ("the
push reached 6.64718 m/s at the track end ... below the release speed"), although it
reached that speed at s of about 12 m. At the 4 m/s corner the window is 1e-7 m/s and
below (1e-6 m/s is found). Every sealed run with a release speed says so in its column
line ("Assumption lines"). No planned variant is affected: lm_fixed's corner equals its
exit speed, and lm_fixed_sealed releases at L. S5 leaves the event as S4a built it; a
scan of the `target_speed` event like *Passed over*'s is a KI candidate.

**Energy** (also "Assist energy identity"). The work done against the column is the
drive's extra state `W_piston_J` (`WORK_STATE`; atol 1e-3 J by its suffix), dW_p/dt =
F_p sdot, so the state vector of a sealed push is [s, sdot, m, W_piston_J, E_drive,
W_thrust, J_mass]; a vented push keeps S4's layout (no extra state). The identity with
the column:

    E_drive + W_thrust = delta(M sdot^2/2 + M g z) - J_mass + dissipated + W_p

W_p is the work done against the column's net force F_p (whose own work on the carriage
is -W_p): drive work the stack does not receive, 4.4% to 5.2% of the supplied work on the
pushes tested, and 1.92 m/s of exit speed on the cold force-law test push (20 t
carriage). The carriage does p_0 A s on the atmosphere above, and the trapped gas gives up
(p_0 V_0 - p V)/(gamma - 1) of internal energy as it expands, so that W_p = p_0 A s -
(p_0 V_0 - p V)/(gamma - 1), the closed form above; the process is reversible in the
model, and W_p is a stated term beside the budget's fields, not dissipated (survey 01
section 6; design section 9: "the piston work is not dissipated").
`losses.PistonWork(work_J, closed_form_J)` holds the quadrature (the summed increments of
`W_piston_J` over the ASSIST phases, `losses.piston_work`) and W_p(s_end) - W_p(s_start);
it is not a field of `AssistEnergyBudget` nor of `sim.Result` (D-SP7-26, D-SP7-27: the
1-D golden dump converts the one field by field and reads the other by attribute), so
the metrics rebuild it from the run's ASSIST phases (`metrics.sealed_shaft_piston`).
`assist_energy_residual_rel` of a sealed push is the identity with W_p
(`assist_identity_residual_rel`); the budget's own `residual_J()` is then W_p (and its
`residual_rel()` about 5%, not a broken identity: the docstrings say so). The efficiency
stays energy-only.

**Metrics** (`SEALED_SHAFT_METRICS`, written after `LINEAR_MOTOR_METRICS` for a sealed
shaft only, 1-D and planar; a vented linear-motor run and every constant_accel run gain
none): `piston_work_J` (the work done against the column, the quadrature W_p),
`piston_force_peak_N` (F_p at the largest s the push's states reach, the release
position for a push that released; F_p rises with s; 0 for a stall),
`bore_pressure_release_pa` (p at the release state, None without a release; the
lowercase `_pa` of `max_q_pa`). The summary's per-variant tables gain `SEALED_SHAFT_ROWS`
after the linear motor's rows when some run is sealed ('-' for the other runs; n/a in
every row of a sealed run with no push record, and in the pressure row of a push that
never released, as the first row's key says); the first row reads "work done against
the trapped column W_p [J] (drive work the stack does not receive: p_0 dV done on the
atmosphere above, less the internal energy the expanding gas gives up; not dissipated
in the model)".

**Assumption lines** (`LinearMotorAssist.assumptions`: thirteen for a sealed shaft, the
vented ten unchanged byte for byte). Under the acceleration law the control line's force
reads "M (a + g_eff sin phi) - (1 - f_imp) T + F_p(s) (the sealed shaft's column)" and a
stop taper's line "at L the drive force is the holding force M g_eff sin phi - (1 -
f_imp) T plus the sealed shaft's column force F_p(L) at the track end", the force the
code flies (the force law's taper is refused). The shaft line opens "linear_motor: shaft
sealed below the carriage (its trapped air column: the three lines that start
'linear_motor: sealed shaft'; above the carriage the shaft is open at the mouth: the
vented shaft named by the track-push line of a planar run is, for this run, that open
shaft above the carriage), no friction", and with a release speed "... named by the
track-push line of a planar run and the early-release line of a release before the track
end is ..." (it names only lines the run can carry; the drag clause as for the vented
shaft: the vehicle above the carriage is in the open shaft). It points to the three
lines by their opening words, not as "the next three lines": summary.md merges the lines
of its runs in order of first appearance, and two sealed runs that differ in the shaft
or column line but share a not-modelled line would break a positional pointer (review
pass 3, P3H-m1). Then three lines (`sealed_assumptions`; the reference numbers in them
are the surveys' cases, labelled so, not this run's):

- the column: the bore, A, the gap, p_0 (the ICAO atmosphere at the track start) and gamma
  ("the bore and the gap assumed; gamma that of air in the ICAO standard atmosphere" when
  gamma is `atmosphere.KAPPA_AIR`, 1.4; else "the bore, the gap and gamma assumed; air in
  the ICAO standard atmosphere has 1.4"), the adiabatic, uniform and quasi-static
  expansion p(s) = p_0 (h_0/(h_0 + s))^gamma, the force on the carriage against the motion
  below its bound p_0 A from push start to the release, its effect by law with its
  conditions ("Where it acts": force law, the drive's force unchanged, the stack slows,
  F_int lower by (m_v/M) F_p and the felt g by F_p/(M g0), the felt g falling on a cold
  push's F_max plateau, the exit speed lower on every push S5's tests and probes measured,
  not guaranteed, or, with a release speed, the release position and the push time larger,
  the speed at release the release speed unless the push reaches the track end first;
  acceleration law, the force and power rise by F_p and F_p sdot while no cap binds and
  the work by W_p and the electricity by W_p/eta while no cap binds on the whole push,
  F_int unchanged, a cap that binds slowing the stack), with a release speed, under
  either law, that the speed of a sealed push can peak inside the track and then fall
  (under a power cap, and under the force law in a slow rise against a gap far below the
  sources' 1 to 20 m) and that a release speed just below such a peak can be passed over
  inside one integrator step (up to 2e-5 m/s below it on the pushes measured), the push
  then releasing at the track end with the flag `release_speed_not_reached` although it
  reached the release speed ("Speed along the stroke"), the work done against the
  column, drive work the stack does not receive (p_0 dV on the atmosphere above, less the
  internal energy the gas gives up), booked beside the identity's terms, not as
  dissipated, and that p_0 A and W_p scale with the bore's area;
- not modelled on the push, each with its direction: the air ahead of the vehicle pushed
  out of the mouth (a momentum flux of the order of rho v^2 A_bore at the exit; survey 08
  A3's case, 76.7 m/s in a 3.7 m bore: about 77 kN, plus 4 to 23 kN at 3 g0 to accelerate
  the air pushed out, 0.4% to 0.5% of a 20.81 MN interface force), which acts on the
  vehicle as the neglected shaft drag does (under the force law it would raise F_int by D
  m_c/M, under the acceleration law by D); the open shaft's hydrostatic drop (F_p biased
  high by up to rho g s sin phi A: 13 kN, 1.2% of F_p(L), for a 3.7 m bore, a 5 m gap and
  a 100 m vertical stroke); the non-uniform, unsteady expansion near the end of a
  small-gap stroke (survey 08 A3's case: the gas has cooled to 35 to 110 K, from about 288
  K, for 0.5 to 10 m gaps, and its sound speed, 118 to 211 m/s, is only 1.5 to 3 times the
  carriage's 76.7 m/s; the uniform adiabat holds that cooling, 85 K at the end of the 5 m
  gap's 100 m stroke), so the uniform, quasi-static adiabat is first order there: the face
  pressure would be lower and F_p nearer its bound, so F_p is biased low there (inferred;
  heat from the walls would act the other way; the bound holds regardless); and, for an
  engine lit on the track, its exhaust, which the sealing carriage leaves only the annulus
  between the bore and the vehicle to escape by (0.231 m^2, 2.15% of a 3.7 m bore around a
  3.66 m body: survey 07's case): the pressure it would build above the carriage, which
  would dominate the push (inferred, not computed), is left out, the thrust and the
  impingement being those of the open shaft (the tests fly hot sealed pushes as checks of
  the identity, not as a model of that exhaust; whether to refuse a sealed shaft lit on
  the track instead is the user's decision);
- not modelled after the release and in the geometry: the trapped column after the release
  (the carriage brakes by its own closed form, the vehicle above it sees the open shaft;
  with a release speed the line says instead that the vehicle is flown so, in the shaft
  open at the mouth after a release at the track end, and that after one before the
  track end the cavity between the departing vehicle's base and the braking carriage,
  which still seals the bore, fed only through the bore-body annulus, is left out: a base
  suction of up to about p_0 A_body, inferred, the vehicle's speed in the shaft after the
  release biased high, and the exhaust of a stage lit before its base clears the mouth,
  trapped there, inferred, the other way: "Push only"), whose pull of up to p_0 A (this
  run's value) would add to the brake's m_c (a_b - g_eff
  sin phi) (0.78 MN for a 5 g0 brake on a 20 t carriage on a vertical track), so the brake
  force, the brake energy and the facility length are upper bounds, a massless carriage
  leaves the column no mass to act on, and a stopped carriage is pulled back down by about
  p_0 A + m_c g_eff sin phi, which the brake would have to hold ("Push only"); the bore
  checked against the diameter sqrt(4 A_ref/pi) of the run's A_ref only (the main-body
  section in the vehicle files), not the vehicle's largest section (the F9 class's 5.2 m
  fairing, 30.0 to 43.1 m below the mouth of a 100 m silo, would not pass a 3.7 m bore; a
  bore that clears it has more than (5.2/3.7)^2 = 1.975 times the area, 3.58 times for the
  7.0 m shaft the scene draws, so more than 1.975 times p_0 A and W_p at the same gap: "The
  bore and the vehicle's largest section"); and that a vented shaft, the alternative,
  needs vents of about the bore area (inferred, survey 07 section 9.2's case: an
  incompressible orifice estimate, C = 0.94 to 0.83, of 11.4 to 13.0 m^2, 1.06 to 1.21 A,
  to hold the pressure difference at the exit dynamic pressure; a 3.7 m bore around a 3.66
  m body is choked, its 0.231 m^2 annulus 2.15% of the bore against the 37.8% Kantrowitz
  minimum at Mach 0.225).

**Closed forms the tests use** (`tests/test_sealed_shaft.py`; the F9 in 1-D through
`fly_track` or `sim.simulate`, g = mu/R_E^2, d = 3.7 m, h_0 = 5 m, gamma = 1.4, p_0 =
p_atm(-100 m), M = m0 + m_c, rtol 1e-11; every expected value from the test's own
formulas):

- p, F_p and W_p against the formulas above for h_0 in {0.5, 1, 5, 20} m and s from 1e-6
  m to 1e4 m: p and F_p at 1e-13 (F_p of its bound), W_p against scipy's adaptive
  quadrature of the plain F_p at 1e-9 relative for s >= 1e-3 m, against the plain closed
  form at 1e-11 for s >= 0.1 m, and against the series W_p = p_0 A gamma s^2/(2 h_0) [1 -
  (gamma + 1) s/(3 h_0)] (good to (s/h_0)^2) within 1e-15 p_0 A s below 1e-3 m; survey
  07's sea-level table to its digits.
- A step force-law push (t_r = 0, P_max never reached), cold: M sddot = F_max - M g sin
  phi - F_p(s), hence (1/2) M v^2 = (F_max - M g sin phi) s - W_p(s) at every step,
  vertical and horizontal, the exit v_e from it, the `W_piston_J` state = W_p(s) at
  every step, and E_drive = (1/2) M v_e^2 + M g sin phi L + W_p(L).
- At the same state (t, s, sdot, m_v, T): the sealed force law's drive force equals the
  vented one's and F_int = F_int,vented - (m_v/M) F_p, the felt g lower by F_p/(M g0),
  cold and hot (both on a 20 t carriage, the hot one with f_imp 0.5); the acceleration
  law's uncapped drive force is the vented one's plus F_p and F_int is unchanged (cold,
  no carriage; hot, a step command no cap reaches, on a 20 t carriage with f_imp 0.5),
  and where the vented command already reaches the cap both sit at it, the drive force
  the same bit for bit and F_int lower by (m_v/M) F_p (the cold push's power cap late in
  the push; a hot step command capped by F_max from push start, no carriage).
- The identity with the column, cold and hot, both laws (the five pushes of
  `_limit_cases`).
- A release at a target speed (the force law cold at 50 m/s, F_max = m0 (3 g0 + g), P_max
  = 50 F_max; no carriage and a 20 t carriage): trigger `target_speed` before L, the exit
  speed the release speed, F_p and p at the flown release position s_release (1e-12) and
  W_p(s_release) (1e-9), the identity with it, the facility max(L, s_release + v^2/(2
  a_b)); against the same drive vented, the release position and the push time larger, and
  the column line saying so, not "the exit speed is lower".
- A speed peak inside the track (the force law cold, no carriage, F_max = m0 (3 g0 + g),
  a 2 m/s power corner): the dense output's largest speed (refined to 1e-12 s) lies at
  1 m < s < L/2, more than 0.1 m/s above the exit speed, with steps where the speed
  falls, and there P_max/sdot = M g + F_p(s) (1e-8; measured 1.1e-9); a release speed 1e-3
  m/s below the peak releases there (`target_speed`), and one 1e-6 m/s below it is
  passed over: the push releases at L, at the exit speed of the push with no release
  speed, with one `release_speed_not_reached` flag ("Speed along the stroke").
- The stall at push start against the column: F_max = M g + F_p(L)/2 stalls (flag
  written out), the same drive vented flies, F_max = (M g + F_p(L))(1 + 1e-3) reaches L,
  and a step push with F_max - M g = 0.95 F_p(L), which would reach L on its momentum, is
  refused (the guard's conservatism, pinned), with a 3 m/s release speed too, its flag
  then adding the early release to what the rule does not credit.

**Measured** (scratch probes, not run by the suite): the step push's speeds on the
energy closed form to 2.4e-15 of v_e (vertical; 1.8e-15 horizontal), its W_piston_J state
on W_p(s) to 4.9e-15 of W_p(L), the exit within 3.3e-16 and E_drive within 2.2e-16, the
same at rtol 1e-10, 1e-11 and 1e-12 (the step cap t_push/push_steps sets the steps); the
identity with the column 1.3e-16 to 1.7e-15 and the quadrature on its closed form
1.3e-15 to 3.0e-15 (the five pushes); the interface share to 2.9e-16 of F_max (both
laws, uncapped and at the cap). The tests assert 1e-9: margins above 1e5. On those
pushes W_p is 4.4% to 5.2% of the push's supplied work (survey 07: 99 MJ of 2.249 GJ,
4.4%, at sea level for the full-load push); the cold force law's push on a 20 t carriage
exits at 67.78 m/s against 69.70 m/s vented, its interface-force peak 20.25 MN against
20.52 MN (test pushes on the 1-D F9, not findings); released at 50 m/s instead, that push
releases at 47.69 m after 2.125 s against 44.89 m after 2.034 s vented (with no carriage
45.41 m after 2.035 s against 42.79 m after 1.950 s), F_p, p and W_p at s_release within
6.7e-15 of the closed forms. The synthetic structural case of
`tests/test_structure_linear_motor.py` (SHORT, 50 m, the synthetic structure file, x =
20 t) sizes 5,812 kg sealed against 5,903 kg vented (n_q 3.966 against 4.019 g0;
synthetic, not a finding).

**Byte identity of the rest.** A vented linear-motor run and every constant_accel run
are byte-identical to the commit before S5: the vented drive keeps no extra state and
S4's arithmetic (the sealed terms are separate branches, never a zero added), no new
metric key, no new summary row, its ten assumption lines; constant_accel is untouched.
`tests/vented_pins_support.py` holds sha256 digests captured from that commit's code
(e12e524: `SOURCE_COMMIT`, the JSON's `source_commit`; its `src` extracted with
`git archive e12e524 src`, never HEAD once S5 is committed; the support module using
only pre-S5 API; the capture reproduced, and the working tree's capture equal to it):

- five 1-D runs (the force law cold and hot on a 20 t carriage, the acceleration law with
  a taper, a release speed, constant_accel 3 g0): their integrator states bit for bit,
  metrics, time series, events, assumption lines, flags, status and budget;
- the planar flown push of S4b's 30 m force-law push (through the config and
  `build_assist`): its phases' states bit for bit, events, flags, status and the drive's
  assumption lines, and its planar track metrics (`planar_track_metrics` on the push, the
  function S5 changed), sampled time series and budget.

The metric key lists (the five 1-D runs and the planar track metrics) are compared
everywhere, the digests in the capture environment (the golden tier's EXACT_ENV_KEYS).
The exact 1-D golden tier, the planar digest pin and output capture and the golden-dump
field lists stand as before.

**Stays out of S5:**

- a partly vented shaft (a pressure state `_pa`, which has no atol entry); heat transfer
  and a non-uniform, unsteady expansion of the column;
- the column after the release and the air above the vehicle (stated, with their
  directions), and the cavity under a vehicle released before the track end, closed below
  by the braking carriage, with the exhaust of a stage lit in it (stated, inferred, with
  their directions: "Push only");
- the exhaust of an engine lit on the track in a sealed shaft (stated; refusing that
  combination instead is the user's decision);
- a scan of the `target_speed` event for an upward crossing passed over at a sealed
  push's speed peak, like *Passed over*'s scan of the two-way watches, or a refusal or
  flag of a sealed release speed on a power-limited push (stated, with the measured
  window: "Speed along the stroke"; a KI candidate);
- a check of the bore against the vehicle's largest section, the bore lm_fixed_sealed
  flies, and whether a sealed variant can sit in a fairing-area bound arm such as
  `aero_bound` (the user's decision before S6b: "The bore and the vehicle's largest
  section");
- the column in the readers. Replay, scene and the app do not name it, and
  `replay.is_vented` reads a sealed block as not vented. On a page with sealed runs only,
  the vented-shaft drag clause and close-up note are left out. On a page with vented and
  sealed runs, the drag clause names the vented runs alone, which implies drag in the
  sealed runs' shaft (there is none above the carriage), and the unnamed close-up note
  ("the shaft is treated as vented") reads as covering the sealed runs. The scene's
  display-only list says "the model has a vented shaft" on every page, and so does the
  shaft note of configs/display/f9_class.yaml. Open: fix them, or refuse a directory with
  a sealed run in the readers, before S6b publishes a sealed page;
- an exact stall rule (the guard above is conservative for every push);
- the experiment variant lm_fixed_sealed (S6b).

## Failed-ignition coast

Modules: `phases/prelude.py` (`IgnitionSpec.fails`,
`flag_ignored_ignition_settings`), `phases/vertical.py` (`VerticalPlanner.ascend` and
`_fail_ignition`), `phases/trace.py` (`RunTrace.failed_stage` / `t_fail_s`), `metrics.py`
(`failed_ignition_metrics`, `last_burn_end_s`, `descent_crossing`,
`carriage_park_altitude_m`, `failed_ignition_flags`), `sim.py`
(`FAILED_IGNITION_ASSUMPTIONS`, `FAILED_IGNITION_TRACK_ASSUMPTIONS`). Test: `tests/test_failed_ignition.py`.

`fails: true` on a stage makes its `ThrustSchedule` identically zero (T_vac = 0, no
mass flow) for the whole run; the config requires `end: impact`, because the only
thing left to compute is where and how fast the vehicle comes down. The run is the
HOLD and ASSIST phases as configured (on a track the engine that fails is simply never
lit: no ignition event, no hold from a negative t_ign, nothing burned before release),
RELEASE, then the terminal coast at once: COAST (sigma = +1, ends at `apex`), FALL
(sigma = -1, ends at `impact` at the ground z = z_ground = 0, which is the silo mouth
in the plan's datum, `exit_altitude_m: 0`), status `impact`. The stage's scheduled
t_ign_s, reference and startup override play no part (there is no COAST_PRE_IGN and
`t_ign_rel_release_s_<stage>` is None); any of them set away from the defaults is
recorded as the run flag `ignition_failed: stage '<name>' has fails: true, so nothing
burns; ignored: ...` so a hot-start-then-fail config is not misread (as long as the
shipped `silo_failed` variant inherits the baseline's t_ign_s = -2 by dict merge it
carries that flag; setting t_ign_s: 0 in the variant would silence it, and the test
allows either). The `ignition_failed` event is logged at the start of the coast with the state
there, in the COAST (or FALL, for a vehicle already falling) phase. A failed *later*
stage does the same from the end of its staging coast, with the mass already staged.
A failed first stage on a pad never lifts off: the hold extends to t_max and the run
ends with status `no_liftoff` ("Hold-down bookkeeping"); `failed_stage` is still
reported and the coast metrics are n/a.

**Closed forms** (release at z = 0 at speed v0 = sqrt(2 a L), the loss identity's
|v_f| - |v_0| = -J_grav with J_vac = J_steer = J_bp = 0):

- Constant g (the analytic device, `ConstantGravity` through `sim.simulate` only):
  h = v0^2/(2 g), t_up = v0/g, back at the mouth at t_return = 2 v0/g with |v| = v0.
  With g = g0 in flight and on the track, h = a L/g0 = 3 L exactly for a 3 g0 push.
- mu/r^2 (the run model): a radial Kepler orbit ("Gravity" and `tests/test_coast.py`)
  with r_a = 1/(1/R_E - v0^2/(2 mu)), a = r_a/2, cos E0 = 1 - R_E/a at the surface,
  t_up = sqrt(a^3/mu) [pi - (E0 - sin E0)], t_return = 2 t_up by time symmetry and
  |v_impact| = v0 by energy conservation; the coast nets no gravity loss (J_grav =
  integral of g sigma dt cancels between the rise and the fall), so speed_end =
  speed_start. Near cos E0 = -1 the acos in that spelling loses ~2e-13 relative in
  double precision (its condition number is ~70 here); the same closed form written
  through delta = pi - E0 = 2 asin(sqrt(h/r_a)), h = r_a - R_E = h_c/(1 - h_c/R_E),
  h_c = v0^2/(2 g_s), g_s = mu/R_E^2, t_up = sqrt(a^3/mu) (delta + sin delta), is
  conditioned to rounding, and the test uses it.
- Shaft bottom (track runs only; derived, not integrated):
  v_bottom^2 = v_impact^2 + 2 g_eff (z_impact - z_track_start), the mirror of the push
  under the track's constant g_eff from the impact point (the ground) down to the
  track start; z_impact - z_track_start = L when the mouth is at the ground, and
  L - exit_altitude in general (the fall between the mouth and the ground is in
  v_impact already, so it is neither double-counted nor missed). The braked carriage
  is in the way, so this is the speed the vehicle *would* have at the track start, a
  bound for what a catch or a crush structure must absorb; no impact with the carriage
  is modelled.
- The carriage (track runs only): after release it brakes along the track tangent and
  parks d_brake = v_exit^2/(2 a_brake) beyond the exit ("Silo model", the run's own
  `braking_distance_m`), at z_carriage = z_exit + d_brake sin phi(L)
  (`metrics.carriage_park_altitude_m`), which for a vertical silo is d_brake above the
  mouth, in the fall-back path. It stops at t = v_exit/a_brake after release (1.56 s
  for the shipped case) while the vehicle, decelerating only at g, is already above
  it; on the way down the vehicle meets it first, before the mouth. Constant g: at
  t_up + sqrt(2 (h - d_brake)/g) at |v| = sqrt(v0^2 - 2 g d_brake); mu/r^2: the time
  from the apex to a drop x below it is sqrt(a^3/mu) (delta + sin delta) with delta =
  2 asin(sqrt(x/r_a)) (the t_up form with x = h), and |v|^2 = v0^2 - 2 mu d_brake /
  (R_E (R_E + d_brake)) by energy. The code reads both off the FALL phase's dense
  output (`metrics.descent_crossing` at z_carriage); it is reported so the mouth and
  shaft-bottom numbers are not mistaken for the first thing the vehicle hits.

**Reported** (`failed_*` metrics, present only when a stage failed; times relative to
release): `failed_stage`; `failed_apex_alt_m` and `failed_t_apex_s`, the highest apex
of the unpowered flight that ends in the failure, i.e. after the last burnout before
it (`metrics.last_burn_end_s`; release for a first stage), so an apex reached inside a
long staging coast before a later stage fails still counts (None when the vehicle was
already falling at that burnout); on a track, `failed_carriage_alt_m`,
`failed_t_carriage_s` and `failed_speed_at_carriage_mps`, where the braked carriage
parks and when and how fast the falling vehicle first comes down to it (None when
the apex is below it, which a carriage braking at less than the vehicle's deceleration
gives, inside the shaft or above the ground; all three None on a pad);
`failed_t_return_s`, when the vehicle is back down
at its release altitude (the mouth, or the pad): the first downward crossing of
z_release after that burn, found by brentq on the FALL phase's dense output
(`metrics.descent_crossing_time_s`), which is the impact event itself when the mouth is at
the ground and None when the ground is above the mouth (a sunken exit: in the 1-D
model the vehicle rises through z = 0 unhindered, a rising phase listing no impact,
and "hits the ground" there on the way back, so that case is a bookkeeping check of
the altitude split, not a consistent geometry; it holds only while the carriage parks at
or above the ground: since SP7 step S4a fix rounds 3 and 4 a buried exit whose carriage
parks below the ground falls back onto it, below), and None after a push released at its
release speed below the ground whose carriage parks at or above the ground (the fall ends
at the ground, above the release altitude; SP7 step S4a fix round 5, P5-m1);
`failed_impact_speed_mps`, |v| at
the impact (the ground); and,
on a track, `failed_speed_at_shaft_bottom_mps` from the formula above. With the mouth
at the ground they duplicate the generic `apex_*` / `impact_*` items under their own
names so a summary can print the failed-ignition line without deciding which apex it
means; with a track exit away from the ground (`exit_altitude_m` is not validated
against 0 in Phase 1) the run flag `failed ignition: the track exit (mouth) is at z =
...` says which altitude each item refers to (`metrics.failed_ignition_flags`; it prints
the planner's ground altitude, not the impact root's 1e-13 m residue).

**Numbers** (F9, 3 g0, L = 100 m, v0 = 76.70717 m/s; `sim.run`, mu/r^2, rtol 1e-10):
apex 300.27024 m at 7.8291233 s after release, the parked carriage (d_brake =
60.000 m above the mouth, a_brake = 5 g0) met at 14.832503 s at 68.61637 m/s, back at
the mouth at 15.6582467 s at 76.70717 m/s, 88.56437 m/s at the shaft bottom (g_eff =
9.7982855 m/s^2). Against the
closed forms in the conditioned (asin) spelling: apex -2.9e-9 m (the test allows
1e-5 m; "Gravity" on what sets that residual), t_up 5.8e-15 relative, t_return -5.4e-12 relative, |v_impact| -1.1e-11
relative, J_grav 8.3e-10 m/s, identity residual -2.8e-14 m/s, the carriage time
-2.9e-12 and speed -6.1e-12 relative. (Against the acos spelling t_up reads -2.4e-13
relative: that is the closed form's own roundoff, not the integrator's.) Under g0
(constant g in flight and on the track): 300.00000 m, 7.8219545 s, the carriage at
14.8181234 s at 68.60898 m/s, 15.6439091 s, 88.57381 m/s at the bottom. The README's
"~300 m, ~7.8 s" are these numbers rounded. Of the 0.27 m the mu/r^2 apex gains over
the g0 one, 0.256 m is g_eff = 9.79829 m/s^2 against g0 = 9.80665 at the surface
(v0^2/(2 g_eff) = 300.256 m) and 0.014 m (h^2/R_E) is the weakening of gravity over the
climb.

**Assumptions added to a failed run whose coast ran** (`FAILED_IGNITION_ASSUMPTIONS`,
plus the carriage lines on a track; a pad `no_liftoff` with `fails: true` never
coasted and gets none of them): the fall-back coast is drag-free (the strings stay generic and
point here for the order of magnitude: at 77 m/s the drag on the F9 class is about
0.4 % of its weight, q = 3.6 kPa on ~10.5 m^2 at C_D ~ 0.5 against 5.3 MN, so the
apex and the return time are good to ~1 %; another vehicle needs its own figure); the
braked carriage parks its braking distance beyond the exit, in the fall-back path, and
the vehicle would meet it there first unless it is withdrawn in time (~14.8 s after
release for the shipped case), no impact with it is modelled, and the return, the
impact and the shaft-bottom speed are the obstacle-free values; the shaft-bottom speed
is derived from the impact speed and the fall from the ground to the track start, not
integrated; no
abort is modelled (a tilted exit that carries the vehicle clear of the mouth is the
planar branch of Phase 2/3); Coriolis drift during the coast is neglected (omega_p =
0), so the vehicle comes straight back down the shaft.

**A fall back inside the shaft** (SP7 step S4a fix rounds 3 and 4, P3-M2, P4-M1;
"Linear motor: the flown power cap, the release at a target speed and the readers",
*After a release below the mouth* and *Over the shaft*). After a release below the
ground whose carriage parks below the ground (a push released at its release speed below
the mouth, or a push to a buried track exit, constant_accel included) the floor of the
flight model in the shaft is the parked carriage (the carriage, braking from the release
at a_b >= the vehicle's deceleration, is parked before the vehicle comes back), and the
coast falls onto it whether its apex lies inside the shaft or above the open mouth (the
coast never kicks, so it stays over the shaft; fix round 4): `failed_t_carriage_s` and
`failed_speed_at_carriage_mps` are the impact's time and speed (`descent_crossing` takes
the phase end within ATOL_M of the carriage as the crossing),
`failed_impact_speed_mps` (at the ground) and `failed_t_return_s` are None (the fall
ends on the carriage, below the ground, whether or not it passed the mouth, and above the
release altitude), and the shaft-bottom speed is the obstacle-free value through the
carriage (from the impact speed and altitude). A carriage braking at less than the
vehicle's deceleration parks above an apex inside the shaft (wherever it parks, below the
ground or above it): the run ends at once at the apex, the carriage items None. Such a run (`metrics.impact_in_shaft`: the impact more
than ATOL_M below the ground) carries the flag `failed ignition: the vehicle fell back
inside the shaft and its impact is at z = ..., on the parked carriage
(failed_t_carriage_s and failed_speed_at_carriage_mps are its time and speed);
failed_impact_speed_mps (at the ground) and failed_t_return_s are None (the fall ends on
the carriage, below the ground, whether or not it passed the mouth, and above the release
altitude), and the shaft-bottom speed is the obstacle-free value through the carriage`
(the apex case: `failed ignition: the vehicle stopped rising inside the shaft and its
impact is at z = ..., at its apex, at or below the parked carriage's altitude (...); ...
and the shaft-bottom speed is the obstacle-free value from the apex, below the
carriage`, fix round 4, H4-m2) in place of the mouth flag, and
`sim.FAILED_IGNITION_SHAFT_ASSUMPTIONS` in place of the two track lines above ("the
floor of the flight model is the braked carriage ... the impact is on it ..., from an
apex inside the shaft or through the open mouth from one above it, or at the apex when
the carriage parks above it; a carriage withdrawn in time is not modelled in the shaft,
any touchdown on the carriage ends the run (no catch and re-hold), and the fall ends
below the ground, above the release altitude ...", and the shaft-bottom speed "derived
from the impact speed (on the carriage, or 0 at the apex) and the fall from the impact
altitude ..., the obstacle-free value, as if the carriage were withdrawn"). A push
released at its release speed whose impact is not inside the shaft (its carriage parks
at or above the ground: the obstacle-free fall to the ground) gets
`sim.FAILED_IGNITION_EARLY_TRACK_ASSUMPTIONS` in place of the two track lines, whose first
says the carriage parks its braking distance "beyond the release point (a push released
at its release speed before the track end; ...), at or above the ground here" (fix round
4: the track line's "beyond the track exit" is false for an early release), that the
vehicle meets it on the way down only "where it parks below the vehicle's apex" (the
carriage items None "when it parks above the apex", as a soft brake parks it), and that
"the impact at the ground and the shaft-bottom speed are the obstacle-free values, and
failed_t_return_s is None after a release below the ground (the fall ends at the ground,
above the release altitude)" (fix round 5, P5-m1, m1, C5-m1: round 4's line called "the
return to the release altitude" an obstacle-free value, None in every such run below the
ground, and no flag says why: `failed_ignition_flags` returns nothing for a mouth at the
ground). 1-D, released at 70 m/s about 16 m down (a = 3 g0, a 5 g0 brake), the carriage
parks 33.5 m above the ground and the vehicle hits the ground 14.050 s after the release
at 67.663 m/s, the quadrature's time and the energy speed (to 1e-12); with a 0.5 g0 brake
at 38.5 m/s the carriage parks 76.6 m above the ground, above the apex 1.1 m above it, and
failed_t_carriage_s is None (`test_a_failed_ignition_after_an_early_release_falls_to_the_ground_past_its_carriage`,
with the planar analogue and `sim.PLANAR_FAILED_IGNITION_EARLY_ASSUMPTIONS`). Every other failed-ignition run keeps the lines, flags
and items above unchanged. The planar failed-ignition coast does the same
(`sim.PLANAR_FAILED_IGNITION_SHAFT_ASSUMPTIONS` in place of the planar line, a run
flagged `shaft_fallback`; `sim.PLANAR_FAILED_IGNITION_EARLY_ASSUMPTIONS`, "... from the
release point of a push released at its release speed before the track end", for an
early release that did not fall back inside the shaft, fix round 4), and its summary
table labels the impact-speed row `summary.PLANAR_SHAFT_IMPACT_LABEL` ("impact speed
|v_rel| at the ground, or inside the shaft after a fall back there (shaft_fallback
flag): on the parked carriage, or at the apex (about 0) when the carriage parks above it
[m/s]", fix round 4, H4-m2) only when one of its runs fell back inside the shaft; the 1-D
labels are unchanged, their cells reading the carriage items and n/a at the ground.

Validation (`tests/test_failed_ignition.py`, every expected value a closed form in the
test): the shipped `silo_failed` variant, resolved from the experiment YAML, through
`sim.run` (apex r_a - R_E to 1e-5 m, t_up from the Kepler form and t_return = 2 t_up
to 1e-9 relative, |v_impact| = v_exit and the shaft-bottom speed to 1e-9 relative,
status `impact`, exactly one apex and one impact event, one `ignition_failed`, no
`ignition`, T_vac = 0 and the mass constant on every row, |J_grav| < 1e-6 m/s, the
carriage at d_brake = braking_distance_m, met at t_up + the Kepler fall of h - d_brake
at the energy speed, both to 1e-9 relative, and no flag other than the
ignored-settings one); the same through `sim.simulate` with `ConstantGravity(g0)` and
g_eff = g0 (apex 3 L, t_up = v0/g0, t_return = 2 v0/g0, the carriage at v0/g0 +
sqrt(2 (h - d)/g0) at sqrt(v0^2 - 2 g0 d), to 1e-9 relative); the mouth 50 m above
the ground (return at 2 v0/g at the mouth, impact at sqrt(v0^2 + 2 g 50) at 2 v0/g +
(v_impact - v0)/g, shaft bottom sqrt(v0^2 + 2 g L) as before, the carriage at 50 +
d_brake, the flag naming z = 50 m and the ground z = 0 m, and the gravity loss
v0 - v_impact < 0, which pins the sign of the integrand) and 30 m below it (the
