`OffloadReport.increments`), `src/launchsim/sim.py` (`payload_structure_transform`,
`offload_pad_load_set`, `offload_structure_inputs`, `central_plausibility`,
`plausibility_factor_for`, `plausibility_end_factor`, `structure_flight_cases`,
`structure_flight_check`, `with_flight_check`, `structure_block_needs_hold` (the
preflight's hold check), `STRUCTURE_PAYLOAD_FLAG`, `STRUCTURE_PAYLOAD_CASE_ASSUMPTION`,
`plausibility_rule_text`, `STRUCTURE_SETS_NOT_IN_FILE`, `FLIGHT_DM_FACTOR_KEY`;
`STRUCTURE_PAYLOAD_CONTRACTION_MAX`, `STRUCTURE_PAYLOAD_RESIDUAL_FRACTION`,
`STRUCTURE_PAYLOAD_FLIGHT_CHECK_NA` and `STRUCTURE_FLIGHT_CHECK_SCOPE` live in `summary`
beside the labels built from them and are re-exported by `sim`), `src/launchsim/structure.py`
(`flight_load_set`, `flight_exceedance`, `FlightCheck`, `FlightElementCheck`,
`FLAG_FLIGHT_EXCEEDANCE`, `FLIGHT_EXCEEDANCE_FLAG_KG`, `FLIGHT_CHECK_ELEMENTS`,
`Plausibility.band_fraction`; `_stage_envelope` and `_barrel_envelope` take the
plate-limited row's anchors),
`src/launchsim/config.py` (`plausibility_scaled` on `StructureSettingsConfig` and
`ResolvedStructureCase`; `offload_solved_run`'s `what`; a block with payload cases needs
an `offload` block), `src/launchsim/summary.py`
(`structure_section`, `STRUCTURE_CASE_ROWS`, `STRUCTURE_PAYLOAD_ROWS` with
`STRUCTURE_PAYLOAD_SETTINGS_ROWS`, `STRUCTURE_ARM_COLUMNS`, `STRUCTURE_ARM_CAVEAT` and
`STRUCTURE_PAYLOAD_RECORD_KIND` (both re-exported by `sim`), `structure_cases_of`,
`structure_layer_label` with `structure_axis_departures`, `structure_row_departures`,
`structure_is_band_end` and `structure_settings_text`, `structure_overrides_text`,
`structure_settings_of`, `structure_flags_text`, `STRUCTURE_SETS_APPLICABILITY`,
`STRUCTURE_LAYER2_ROWS_LABEL`, `STRUCTURE_SETTINGS_ROWS_LABEL`,
`STRUCTURE_FLIGHT_CHECK_ROW_LABEL`, `STRUCTURE_FLIGHT_CHECK_NOTE`,
`STRUCTURE_FLIGHT_CHECK_SCOPE`, `STRUCTURE_FLIGHT_CHECK_SCOPE_SHORT`,
`STRUCTURE_FLAGS_NOT_SIZED`,
`STRUCTURE_ELEMENT_NOT_IN_PATH`, `STRUCTURE_PAYLOAD_NOT_WRITTEN`,
`STRUCTURE_PAYLOAD_FLAG_NA`, `STRUCTURE_PAYLOAD_NO_FULL_LOAD`,
`STRUCTURE_PAYLOAD_OFFLOADS_NOTHING`),
`src/launchsim/plots.py` (`structure_figure`, `write_structure_figure`),
`src/launchsim/units.py` (`n_to_mn`, `mn_to_n`) and `src/launchsim/cli.py` (the payload
cases' console lines). Tests: `tests/test_structure_reporting.py` (the synthetic file and
the synthetic pad; fake passes; nothing solved on a pre-registered case, D-SP7-31). Design
4.2 (the flight check), 4.2.5, 4.4 ("Payload form", "Records", "Summary", "Figures"),
D-SP7-18, D-SP7-19, D-SP7-32, D-SP7-33, D-SP7-41; phase file SP7 section 12, deviation 17.
Every row, column, figure and metric key of this section exists only on a structural run or
when the experiment declares a structure block, so the planar output capture and every
SP1-type record, summary and sweep index are unchanged (the tests of
tests/test_planar_pipeline.py and tests/test_offload_pipeline.py pin them).

**The payload form** (design 4.4; `_structure_payload_case`). A payload case `{name, of,
set, ...}` of the structure block flies its variant at its own payload capacity P* with the
structure sized for its full-load push, on the transform of `payload_structure_transform`
(the envelope from the reference pad's own flight, the geometry from the variant at its full
loads, the sizing basis full_load, so the transform never offloads). Two passes:

    dm_0 = S(P_ref)             the full-load sizing at the pad's P_ref;
    P_1* = search(m + dm_0)     the payload search on the vehicle carrying dm_0;
    dm_1 = S(P_1*)              the full-load sizing at P_1*;
    P_2* = search(m + dm_1)     the payload search on the vehicle carrying dm_1.

Each pass's run is the variant with dm restated under the structure's provenance
(`config.offload_solved_run` at an offload of 0: no propellant removed, each stage's dry
mass gaining its dm with the `source` of "Verification with dm" and a note prefixed
`structure payload case <name>`, its `what`, never the solved case's `offload case <name>
(solved)`: nothing is solved here), run through the pass's memo under the structure key, so a second pass whose dm equals the first's to the bit
reuses the first's search. The recorded run is the P_2* search's run, named after the case,
carrying dm_1; the first pass's run is a checked run (its per-run checks listed, nothing of
it written). The passes are not iterated further; the sizing's residual at P_2* is
estimated, never measured, from the two passes' contraction

    c = |(P_2* - P_1*)/(dm_1 - dm_0)| x |(dm_1 - dm_0)/(P_1* - P_ref)|,

the product of the search's sensitivity to dm and the sizing's sensitivity to the payload
(c = |P_2* - P_1*| / |P_1* - P_ref| when dm_1 != dm_0; 0 when the second pass flew the
first's vehicle; inf, so the flag fires, when P_1* = P_ref with a moved sizing), and the
residual estimate c |P_2* - P_1*| (the next pass would move P* by about that much). The
flag `structure_payload_unconverged` fires when the estimate exceeds
`STRUCTURE_PAYLOAD_RESIDUAL_FRACTION` = 0.5 times `final_payload_xtol_kg` or c exceeds
`STRUCTURE_PAYLOAD_CONTRACTION_MAX` = 0.1 (both constants in `summary`, which builds the
payload table's two labels from them, re-exported by `sim`); it is promoted to the run's
flags like the structure flags. The record (kind `STRUCTURE_PAYLOAD_RECORD_KIND`,
"structure payload case") goes to the offload record's `structure_payload_cases` list,
never under `cases`: `name`, `kind`, `of`, `reference_payload_kg`, `dm_0_kg` and
`dm_0_stage2_kg`, `pass_1_run`, `payload_1_kg`, `search_1_status`, `run`, `run_status`,
`status` (ok, or the failed search's), `dm_1_kg` and `dm_1_stage2_kg`, `payload_kg` (P_2*),
`payload_delta_kg` (P_2* - P_ref), `payload_2_minus_1_kg`, `contraction`,
`residual_estimate_kg`, `residual_tolerance_kg`, `unconverged`, `vs_pad`, `flight_check`
(the text `STRUCTURE_PAYLOAD_FLIGHT_CHECK_NA`: the post-hoc flight check is not run on a
payload case, see "The post-hoc flight check"), `flags`, then the run-level structure keys
of the second sizing (`structure_record` with dm_1 at x*, the mass the run carries, so its
`structure_dm_kg` is dm_1, and with dm_0 as the sizing at x = 0, so its `structure_dm_x0_kg`
is the full-load sizing at P_ref, the same quantity an offload case of the same variant and
settings records under that key; its `structure_flight_exceedance_kg` stays null and no
flight flag is appended). The run carries `STRUCTURE_PAYLOAD_CASE_ASSUMPTION` (ending with
the same not-applicable words) and the structure assumption line ("Assumptions"). A block
with payload cases needs an `offload` block (the payload form runs inside the offload pass
against its reference pad and P_ref): `config.ExperimentConfig` refuses one without, so
the cases are never silently dropped. A
payload case whose variant did not run is noted OFFLOAD_NOT_RUN; a search that finds no P*
on either pass ends the case with that search's status: `run` null, nothing written, no
figure, `unconverged` null and no payload flag (a failed second pass keeps dm_1 and the
structure keys on the record, its `payload_kg` the search's NaN), and the summary's payload
table prints the status of both passes, STRUCTURE_PAYLOAD_NOT_WRITTEN for the run and
STRUCTURE_PAYLOAD_FLAG_NA for the flag. The fired flag's run line carries c, the residual
estimate and the tolerance. Measured by hand on 2026-10-11 by running SP1's experiment with
the synthetic file at the shipped budget (silo_cold; not pinned by a test, not a finding):
dm_0 5,784.6 kg, P_1* 26,516.1 kg, dm_1 5,790.5 kg, P_2* 26,515.1 kg, c 0.0022, the residual
estimate 0.0023 kg against the tolerance 0.025 kg (not flagged).

**The block-level `structure_inputs`** (`offload_structure_inputs`; beside
`energy_inputs`, only with a structure block): the file's path and sha256; the envelope pad
and P_ref; `envelope`, per element of both stages the required thickness's maximum over its
stations [m], that station's index and height, its governing mode and its governing load
case (index, label and time; none at the minimum gauge), at the central coefficients, margin
0 and no cap on the reference pad (`envelope_basis` says so; a case with a margin or a cap
has its own envelope); `plausibility`, the rule's table on that envelope (the element
masses, M_model on the physical and the cylinder-equivalent lengths, the length ratios, R
and its per-tank form, the band's edges and `band_fraction` (the file's
`heineman_band_fraction`, carried by `Plausibility`), M/R, the factor on each end, the
rule's text `plausibility_rule_text` at that band (the edges printed from it, never an
assumed 0.7 and 1.3), `dominant` (the rule's trigger, computed from the envelope: the
stage-1 tank element carrying the largest share of M_model, its share, and the governing
mode, load case label and height of its thickest station in the envelope the rule reads)
and the quantities printed beside: Akin's fractions, the interstage relation, k_ts T_max,
stage 1 less its engines); `sets`, the frozen sets as the file records
them (label, source, method, evaluation count, fallbacks, seed, parent commit, reproducing
test; per set its values, searches, implied stack length, each polish's passes and dm before
and after with its moves counted, each extremality check) with `sets_label` =
`structure.SEARCH_LABEL`; `tornado` and `break_even` null with `tornado_note` =
`STRUCTURE_SETS_NOT_IN_FILE`: the structure file freezes neither (its `sets.method` says
search D is not frozen there; S2's sizing-only tornado and break-even estimates live in the
phase file's session log), so the record says so instead of quoting a number from elsewhere:
a deviation from design 4.4's record list ("the tornado, the axes' break-even values"),
logged in the phase file's section 12; adding them to the frozen file is a change to
configs/structures, which D-SP7-31 governs before S6a.

**The plausibility-scaled row** (D-SP7-33 applied as approved, D-SP7-41). A case with
`plausibility_scaled: true` (physics_low_mass or physics_high_mass only) multiplies every
sizing's dm by the rule's factor for its band end, inside the fixed point, so the scaled mass
is the mass flown and the push it sizes is the push of that mass:

    (dm1, dm2)_{k+1} = f S(push(m(x) + dm_k)),

f = (1 + b) R / M on physics_low_mass when M > (1 + b) R (else 1), (1 - b) R / M on
physics_high_mass when M < (1 - b) R (else 1), with b the structure file's
`heineman_band_fraction` (0.30 in the shipped files, 0.3 in the synthetic one; never an
assumed 0.7 and 1.3), M the model's envelope tank mass and R Heineman's relation at
the central coefficients on the pad's envelope (`central_plausibility`: margin 0, no cap,
stage 1; the rule's basis, computed from the envelope at run time and never typed in; for an
arm the perturbed pad's). The record keys `structure_plausibility_ratio` (M/R),
`structure_plausibility_factor` (the end's factor; 1.0 when the rule does not fire on that
end or the set is not a physics end) and `structure_plausibility_scaled` are on every
structural run; a scaled run's `structure_elements`, `structure_closed_form_kg` and
`structure_ring_kg` carry the factor, so they sum to dm; its provenance (the restated dry
mass's `source`, the assumption line) ends with ", plausibility-scaled" and its memo key
differs from the unscaled case's. Measured on the synthetic file and pad at the headline
offload: f = 0.8456 (M/R 1.5374), the scaled dm 0.8451 times the unscaled (the fixed point
moves it by 0.05%).

**The post-hoc flight check** (design 4.2: "The recorded assisted run's own flight is
checked after the solve against the same envelope; any exceedance is sized and reported
beside dm (not iterated)"). After a structural offload case's recorded run is assembled
(the solve at P_ref), `structure_flight_check` reads its rows after the release with the
flight-only adapter `structure_flight_cases` (the pad adapter refuses a Result with a
push, so its contract is unchanged): every stage-1 row with an engine lit (phase in
`LIT_KINDS`, which excludes HOLD and ASSIST) and every stage-2 burn row, as FLIGHT cases with
the masses recovered as the pad adapter recovers them on the run's own vehicle (the
offloaded loads, the dry masses carrying dm, the payload it flew), checked against the
vehicle (the first flight mass at most the full stack, stage 1's propellant 0 at its
depletion event). `structure.flight_load_set` prepares them (no HOLD case; MECO the last
stage-1 row) and `structure.flight_exceedance` evaluates, per element of
`FLIGHT_CHECK_ELEMENTS` (the two barrels, the three domes and the tube of stage 1, and of
stage 2 when the push sized it), the required thickness under the flight's cases by the
envelope reduction itself (`_stage_envelope` at unit load factor: quasi-static, drag left
out, the pad's own treatment) with the flight's stage-1 felt n capped as the envelope's was
(`PadLoadSet.features` at the envelope's `envelope_cap_g`; stage-2 rows are never capped,
as on the pad), so on a capped case the pad's own unthrottled loads above the cap (5.2 g0
at MECO against a 4.5 g0 cap) are not reported as the push's; the flight is evaluated
unfactored (as the push is sized) against the envelope at the case's margin, so a margin
row's check fires only above the margin's headroom (a flight at +5% felt n exceeds the
synthetic pad's envelope at margin 0 and stays inside it at margin 0.1); under a
plate-limited stiffened row the flight's barrel is anchored at the pad envelope's design
compression N_env, as the push sizing anchors it (`_barrel_push`; `_stage_envelope` and
`_barrel_envelope` take the anchors), so the flight follows the push's linear law
t_ref(N_env) N / N_env and not the anchor row's power law at the flight's own load, which the
reduction uses for the pad envelope itself and which under-reports a plate-limited
exceedance (the synthetic physics_high_mass set at +5% n: 94.5 kg on the RP-1 barrel against
the push-consistent 159.5 kg; the central set and the monocoque LOX barrel are unaffected);
it sizes the positive part over the transform's envelope as the push increment is sized (per
station 2 pi r rho dz x the factor by the flight's governing mode, each station's whole cell
at its mode's factor without the push's cell split at a factor switch; domes and the tube
area x rho x their factor), summed and never iterated. The exceedance is the unscaled sizing:
a plausibility-scaled case's dm carries the rule's factor and its exceedance does not; the
flag's values carry that factor under `sim.FLIGHT_DM_FACTOR_KEY` (1.0 on an unscaled case)
and the flag line and the summary row say so.
The aft skirt and the ring are not checked: the skirt's flight load is the thrust path,
equal on the pad and on the assisted run to the engines' inertia, and its envelope path is a
modelling choice (D-SP7-17), so an exceedance there would charge the assist for a load the
pad's own flight carries; the ring is new hardware sized to the push alone. Every place
the mass is printed states this scope (`summary.STRUCTURE_FLIGHT_CHECK_SCOPE`: "the tank
elements with a station envelope only: the barrels, the domes and the tube; the aft skirt
and the load ring are not checked", in full in the note under the table and in the flag
line, and in short in the case table's row label, `STRUCTURE_FLIGHT_CHECK_SCOPE_SHORT`:
"tank elements only, not the aft skirt or the ring", so the label stays under 160
characters and the table's first column keeps its width, visual V7), so a printed 0 never
reads as a clearance of the whole structure; the flag
line prints "stage 2 not checked (not sized by the push)" rather than "stage 2 0 kg" when
stage 2 was not checked. The total goes
into `structure_flight_exceedance_kg` beside dm (`with_flight_check`), and
`structure_flight_exceedance` is appended to `structure_flags` with its numbers (total,
stage 1, stage 2, the threshold, the cases checked, whether stage 2 was, the margin, the cap
(NaN for none; the flag line and the summary note say both treatments), and per element),
fired above `FLIGHT_EXCEEDANCE_FLAG_KG` = 1 kg and then promoted to the run's flags. A run
without a time series (a solve that recorded no flight; a test's fake run) leaves the key
null and adds no flag. The check is not run on a structure payload case
(`STRUCTURE_PAYLOAD_FLIGHT_CHECK_NA`, on the record under `flight_check`, in the run's
assumption line and in the payload table): its run flies its own P_2* while the envelope is
the pad's at P_ref, so a check against it would measure the payload gain P_2* - P_ref (a
heavier upper mass at the same MECO n, which the pad's own flight at P_2* would need just as
much), not the push; measured in the third review of this step on SP1's experiment with the
synthetic file: the pad itself flown at the silo's P* (27,553 kg) against its own P_ref
envelope needs 7.65 kg, the silo at that payload 7.97 kg, the push's share about 0.3 kg
below the 1 kg threshold, so the flag would have fired on every payload gain above roughly
+0.2 t. Comparing against the pad's own flight at P_2* would cost a further pad flight per
case; the design and the step name the recorded structural run of the solve at P_ref, where
the payload is equal and the check isolates the offload and dm, so the payload cases are
marked not applicable instead. Measured by hand on 2026-10-11 by running SP1's experiment
with the synthetic file at the shipped budget (silo_cold, the central set; not pinned by a
test): the recorded structural run's flight gives 0.0 kg on every element over the 10,443
lit rows after the release (the check's `cases`; the series has 10,731 rows; the offloaded
stack's heads and loads stay inside the full-load pad's envelope); a test flies the synthetic
pad flight at 20% more felt n and sees the exceedance and the flag, and the same flight with
1,500 kg more payload (its masses shifted alike) exceeding the P_ref envelope, the payload
gain the check would have charged to a payload case. The preflight (`sim.check_resolved`,
`structure_block_needs_hold`) refuses a structure block whose reference pad does not light
stage 1 before its hold-down release (lit at or after it, at a height, or never): the pad's
HOLD rows build the skirt's hold-down envelope (`structure.pad_load_set`), and only a pad lit
before its release holds down with the thrust above the weight, the restrained-thrust case.
A pad lit at or after the release holds, if at all, through the liftoff extension at TWR < 1
(`prelude.hold_until_liftoff`; measured in the third review's follow-up on the shipped pad
with the 2 s startup ramp: lit at 0 s it holds 1.5 s and flies 4 HOLD rows, lit at -0.01 s
6, lit at -2 s 5), whose HOLD rows carry the weight alone, so its envelope would lack that
case; with a step startup lit at or after the release there is no HOLD row at all and
`pad_load_set` raises. The refusal is a modelling choice of the structural reference,
stricter than the pass's own requirement of one HOLD row (it refuses the ramp case too),
and its message says how the pad lights and why that is refused, never that the pad flies no
HOLD phase; it comes before any run directory exists rather than after the nominal runs
have flown.

**The Structure subsection** (`summary.structure_section`; `### Structure`, inside the
offload section after the cases table and before the decomposition, only when the record
carries `structure_inputs`): a line naming the file, its sha256, the envelope pad and P_ref,
and that every dm is the model's first-order station sizing charged to the assisted run only
(the pad keeps its vehicle, D-SP7-35); the case table (`STRUCTURE_CASE_ROWS`, one column per
structural case with SP1's penalty rows of the same experiment beside, `structure_cases_of`):
the assisted run, the kind (modelled structure, or the assumed penalty: a parametric row,
not a sized structure), the layer and set (`structure_layer_label`, by D-SP7-18 and design
4.2.6: at the headline settings, flown, rise_time, aft_ring, margin 0, no cap and no
overrides, D-SP7-18's three layers by `STRUCTURE_LAYER_LABELS`, the outer sets as "the
design axes at their corner, the physics coefficients searched", the central layer-1 label
only for the central set at those settings; a case that moves a design axis, a margin above
0, an envelope cap, a dynamic mode other than rise_time or any override
(`structure_axis_departures`; the margin and cap never count on an outer set, which records
its own) prints "design axis (layer 2): <set> at margin m, cap c g0, dynamic d with
overrides <path value; ...>", never the set's own label, D-SP7-43; a case that moves only
the entry path or the sizing basis (`structure_row_departures`, design 4.2.6's "rows, not
band") prints "<layer label>, a row, not a band end (entry e, sizing s): <set>"; a payload
case's full_load basis is the payload form's own and not a departure), the
design-axis overrides row (`structure_overrides_text`: the overrides, `none`, or n/a on a
penalty row), the sizing basis, the dynamic mode with t_r, f and the DLF, n_q, n_peak, F_peak
[MN] (`units.n_to_mn`), the ramp cost, the entry, the margin, the cap, whether the dm is
plausibility-scaled with M/R and the end's factor (a number on the two physics sets, "n/a
(not a band end)" on the central and the outer sets), dm1 (dm - dm2) and dm2 at x* (their labels
saying a no_offload end was sized at x = 0, `STRUCTURE_AT_X_NOTE`), dm at x = 0, the penalty
rows' assumed mass (the offload cases table's own words), the status, x* [t] and the share of
the stage-1 load (a no_offload end prints `STRUCTURE_NO_OFFLOAD_CELL` in both, never "0 t" or
0, D-SP7-32), the verification's P* - P_ref and whether it passed, the flight check's
exceedance (`STRUCTURE_FLIGHT_CHECK_ROW_LABEL`: the quantity, its unit and the element
scope in short, `STRUCTURE_FLIGHT_CHECK_SCOPE_SHORT`, not the aft skirt or the ring; the
full scope sentence, its qualifications, the cap treatment, the
unfactored flight at the case's margin, the unscaled sizing beside a scaled row's dm, n/a
without a time series and not applicable to a payload case, are the note printed under the
table, `STRUCTURE_FLIGHT_CHECK_NOTE`), the fixed-point sizings, the fired structure flags
(`structure_flags_text`: their names, `none`, or `STRUCTURE_FLAGS_NOT_SIZED` for a
search_failed solve, where no sizing at x* was made and no flag evaluated)
and the flag count; one line per no_offload end (`_no_offload_line`): the solver's
`dv_shortfall_mps` at x = 0 and the payload deficit P_2* - P_ref of the payload case of the
same variant and settings (`structure_settings_of`: set, dynamic mode, entry, margin, cap,
overrides and whether plausibility-scaled) when one was flown, else "not flown", naming a
same-set payload case whose other settings differ with what differs rather than quoting it;
the physics band and the outer envelope each on a line (`_band_line`, `_band_end`: each end
named and bracketed, "x* at the low-mass end [...]; at the high-mass end [...]", so a scaled
end's factor is never read as running to the other end; at each end every case of that set
at the headline settings (`structure_is_band_end`: no design-axis departure and no entry or
sizing departure; the plausibility-scaled twin of an end is an end too), the unscaled cases'
x* and, beside them, each plausibility-scaled case's x* with its factor, so the unscaled and
the scaled ends stand side by side, D-SP7-41; a set with a scaled case only says "scaled
only ... the unscaled end was not flown"; an unscaled end whose rule fired with no scaled
twin says "the rule's factor on this end is f; no plausibility-scaled case was flown"; a
no_offload end as such; an end the experiment did not fly as "not flown"; the
sets' label, the file's source, evaluation count, parent commit and reproducing test); the
design-axis break-even line quoting `tornado_note`; the layer-2 line (`_layer2_line`,
`STRUCTURE_LAYER2_ROWS_LABEL`: every case that moves a design axis, named with its base
set, what it moves and its x* (`_xstar_phrase`: "x* 15 t (name, status ok)", a no_offload
end as "no offload (...)", a search_failed solve as "no x* (name, status search_failed)",
never "n/a t" or "x* no"), "never a band end", so the band lines and the case table's
"design axis (layer 2)" cell agree; absent when none ran) and the settings-rows line
(`_settings_rows_line`, `STRUCTURE_SETTINGS_ROWS_LABEL`: every physics- or outer-set case
kept off its band for moving only the entry path or the sizing basis; absent when none
ran); where the sets were found (the
file's `sets.method` verbatim: the one push the search sized at) and the applicability line
(`STRUCTURE_SETS_APPLICABILITY`, design 4.2.6: the sets behind the ends are the extremes in
dm the search found, sizing only, at that one push; each x* on a band line is this
experiment's own solve with that set; a case whose push is not the search's reads its set as
the headline's sets applied to this push, not as this push's extreme; the frozen file records
the search's push in prose only, so the line is printed on every run rather than computed per
case); the element table of the central case (the
first central case at the headline settings, else the first central case at the headline's
design axes, else the first central case, named "the central case <name>" only at the
headline settings and otherwise "the central-set case <name> (<what it moves>; not the
headline settings)", `_central_case_phrase`, in the heading and the trigger line alike; at
x*, or at x = 0 for a no_offload end) with how each element was sized under the case's
entry (`_element_how`: a station sizing over the pad envelope for the barrels, the skirt,
the domes and the tube; the interstage's mass-estimating relation scaled by the Gerard
exponent; the thrust-structure relation as the code applies it, k_ts max(0, F_peak + T - (1
+ margin) T_max) with T the thrust at the push's peak, under entry thrust_structure, and
"not in the load path on entry aft_ring" otherwise; the ring frame in closed form with no
envelope credit under entry aft_ring and "not in the load path on entry thrust_structure"
otherwise, `STRUCTURE_ELEMENT_HOW` and `STRUCTURE_ELEMENT_NOT_IN_PATH`), the station-sized
and relation elements' sum (`structure_closed_form_kg`), the ring's sum and dm1 + dm2; the
pad envelope per element (`_envelope_table`, mm by `units.m_to_mm`); the plausibility table
with the band fraction and its edges printed from the record, the rule and its trigger line
(`_plausibility_trigger`: where M/R lies against the band and which end's factor follows, the
element carrying the largest share of M_model with its share, governing mode, load case and
station, and the central case's own push increment on that element, or that no central case
was flown); the payload cases table (`STRUCTURE_PAYLOAD_ROWS`: the recorded run, the status
of the P_2* search and of the P_1* search, then the settings that sized dm_0 and dm_1
(`STRUCTURE_PAYLOAD_SETTINGS_ROWS`: the layer and set, the overrides, the sizing basis, the
dynamic mode with t_r, f and the DLF, n_peak and F_peak at P_1*, the entry, the margin, the
cap, whether plausibility-scaled with M/R and the end's factor, the same cells as the case
table's, so a scaled physics-set payload case never reads like a central one), P_ref, dm_0,
P_1*, dm_1, P_2*, P_2* - P_ref, P_2* - P_1*, c, the residual estimate, its tolerance, the
flag, the flight check's row printing `STRUCTURE_PAYLOAD_FLIGHT_CHECK_NA`) under a heading
that names, for each payload case, the full_load rows of the same variant and settings
(`structure_settings_of`) or `STRUCTURE_PAYLOAD_NO_FULL_LOAD`, and says these runs
offload nothing, P_2* - P_ref being the payload change at the full load, not a propellant
saving (`STRUCTURE_PAYLOAD_OFFLOADS_NOTHING`); the structural arms' count on one bullet and
`STRUCTURE_ARM_CAVEAT` as the next (deviation 17: an
arm is sized on its perturbed vehicle and on the pad its offload was solved against, its
perturbed pad for a vehicle parameter and the unchanged pad for a run parameter, not on
perturbed station masses; under the stage-1 dry-mass arm the perturbed dry mass reaches the
sizing only through the interface force and the perturbed pad's envelope, measured +10.4 kg
of dm for +10% on the synthetic file); and the figures named (`STRUCTURE_FIGURES_TEXT`: the
stations of stage 1 and, where the push sized stage 2, of stage 2), plots/<run>_structure.png
per structural run. The arms table of the offload section gains `STRUCTURE_ARM_COLUMNS` (dm
at x*, the set, the arm's own envelope pad) when some arm is structural, with the same caveat
printed under it; an arm that was never solved (its same-perturbation pad has no P*) prints
"n/a (not solved: <status>)" in them, an arm of an unstructured case "n/a (uncharged)". The
existing caveats and labels of the offload section are S3a's to reword and are unchanged
here.

**The sweep and arm columns.** `OFFLOAD_STRUCTURE_SWEEP_COLUMNS` (`structure_set`,
`structure_sizing`, `structure_dynamic`, `structure_entry`, `structure_margin`,
`structure_cap_g`, `structure_dm_kg`, `structure_dm_stage2_kg`, `structure_dm_x0_kg`,
`structure_dlf`, `structure_n_peak_g`, `structure_F_peak_N`, `structure_ramp_cost_rel`,
`structure_plausibility_factor` (the end's factor on the two physics sets; null on the
central and the outer sets, which are not band ends, so a 1.0 is never read as "the rule did
not fire" there), `structure_flags`: the fired flags' names "; "-joined, `none` when none,
`STRUCTURE_FLAGS_NOT_SIZED` for a search_failed solve; `structure_plausibility_scaled`,
`structure_overrides`, the overrides as `<path> <value>; ...` or `none` by
`summary.structure_overrides_text`, and `structure_plausibility_ratio`, M_model / R on every
point, so a sweep point's dm has its basis on disk: whether the factor is applied, which
coefficients were overridden and the rule's state, since a sweep point writes no case
record) are written `<case>.<column>`
to sweep_index.csv after every case's
`OFFLOAD_SWEEP_COLUMNS` group and before `status`, only for a case that was structural at
some point of the sweep (`offload_structure_index_values`; the KI-028 pattern: appended, so
every earlier column keeps its name and place, and an SP1-type sweep's index is unchanged byte
for byte); the sweep summary prints the frame as it is. The three columns beyond the step's
list, `structure_plausibility_scaled`, `structure_overrides` and
`structure_plausibility_ratio`, are logged in the phase file's section 12. A sweep point's
resolved_config.yaml carries the block's structure file as
its last key `structure` only when a structural case was solved at that point (the sweep
names one and offload is on: the run path's own rule, the key naming a file a run at that
point used; `structure_block_used`, `write_single`'s `structure`, `_run_sweeps_into`), and no
key otherwise: not with `--no-offload`, not at a point of a sweep naming only plain cases,
never on the `baseline/` copy or a paired pad's. A
structural sensitivity arm's record in `offload.sensitivity[]` ends with
`STRUCTURE_RECORD_KEYS` (its `structure_envelope_pad` naming its own perturbed pad for a
vehicle parameter), so the arm is marked structural on disk; the caveat is printed beside the
arms, not stored per arm.

**The figure** (`plots.structure_figure`, written by `write_run` as
plots/<run>_structure.png for every run of `OffloadReport.increments`, a structural case's
recorded run or a payload case's, when plots are on, from that run's case record
(`structure_figure_record`: the offload or payload case whose `run` it is, so the figure knows
the case's status, x* and kind; the station profiles stay in memory and are not written to
metrics.json). Two panels. The top (`_draw_elements`, `_mark_modes`, `_label_elements`): the
required wall thickness [mm]
against the station height z [m] above the stage-1 load ring (the stack frame) of every
stage-1 element with stations (the aft skirt, both barrels; a dome or the tube as one
labelled push point joined by a drop line in the stage colour to the hollow square of its
envelope, the square drawn on top with a thin edge so it shows when the two coincide; two
point elements at one station height, the aft dome and the tube, set
`STRUCTURE_COINCIDENT_OFFSET_PT` apart on the page, `_z_offsets_pt`, so neither hides the
other's square; a line drawn through that page-offset transform enters no data limit,
matplotlib's autoscale reads transData lines only, so each point element's data
coordinates are added to its axes' limits by hand, `update_datalim`, and the stage-2
inset's z range covers the pair at its lowest station rather than starting at the first
barrel), the pad envelope dashed, the push as a line in the stage's colour, the
push's governing mode marked by a colour and a marker shape fixed per mode name
(`STRUCTURE_MODE_MARKERS`, keyed by the model's mode names so a mode keeps its colour and
shape across every figure of a results directory; a palette disjoint from the stage colours)
and thinned on a dense barrel to `STRUCTURE_MARKER_SPACING_PX` = 20 px (every mode switch and
both ends always marked, `_marked_stations`) so at least a marker's width of push line shows
between the marks; every element label placed once the layout is final (`_place_label`): at
the first anchor and offset (a point element at its point, a barrel at its push's maximum
then along its stations, `_label_anchors`; the offsets `STRUCTURE_LABEL_OFFSETS_PT` above
and below first, then farther out) whose text box, padded by `STRUCTURE_LABEL_PAD_PX`,
covers no drawn station, envelope point or drop-line sample of any element, overlaps no
placed label and not the governing annotation's box, stays inside its axes and off the
stage-2 inset; when no offset is clear (a crowded inset), at the nearest clear position of
the grid `STRUCTURE_LABEL_FAR_FRACTIONS` with a thin leader line to its anchor
(`_far_candidates`, `STRUCTURE_LABEL_LEADER`); else at the candidate of the least cost
(`STRUCTURE_LABEL_COSTS`); the legend
under the panel outside the plotting area in two columns, built from synthetic handles with
self-contained entries (the envelope dashed, "at the case's margin and cap": a margin or a
cap row's envelope is its own; one line per stage drawn; the push point "on a drop line"; the
envelope square named as such, `STRUCTURE_LEGEND_POINT_ENVELOPE`, since the legend fills
column-major and the entry need not follow the push point's; one entry per mode drawn)
independent of the order the elements were drawn in (`_thickness_legend`); the record's
governing element and
station annotated with its push and envelope thickness in a box with a leader arrow, placed
before the element labels (it has the fewer places to go) at the first of
`STRUCTURE_ANNOTATION_CANDIDATES` (the corners, then the mid positions, in
axes fraction) whose box covers no drawn station or envelope point and not
the stage-2 inset, else at the one of least cost (`STRUCTURE_ANNOTATION_COSTS`; the texts
measured on the figure's Agg renderer after the layout, `_place_annotation`); where the push
sized stage 2, its elements drawn in an inset at the top right (`STRUCTURE_STAGE2_INSET_RECT`)
with its own z range, the panel's z range extended past stage 1's data
(`STRUCTURE_STAGE2_X_EXTENSION`) so the inset covers no stage-1 station, the inset given its
final position before the labels are placed (`_settle_inset`: an inset axes is placed by its
locator at draw time, so its transform would otherwise be stale for the overlap tests), the
axis label saying
"stage 2 in the inset"; otherwise the axis label and the caption saying stage 2 was not sized
(no stage-2 station is drawn; the summary's figures line says the same). The title's second
line (the layer label and set) is wrapped at `STRUCTURE_TITLE_WRAP_CHARS`, so the outer sets'
long labels never run past the figure's edge. The bottom (`_dm_panel`): dm by element from the
record's `structure_elements` [kg], bars by stage, the ring frame hatched, each bar labelled
with its kg, the axis label saying how the elements were sized under the case's entry
(`_dm_axis_label`, the rule of `summary._element_how`: under aft_ring the thrust structure
"not in the load path on entry aft_ring, 0 by construction" and the hatched ring frame in
closed form; under thrust_structure the interstage and the thrust structure by their
relations and "no ring frame on entry thrust_structure: the ring frame's 0 is by
construction"; never a relation the entry does not apply), a plausibility-scaled case's
factor in the title. The title names the case and its set's layer label
(`structure_layer_label`); the caption names the layer and set and the case settings (it
asserts nothing about how the set was found: the summary's band lines carry the sets' label
with the file's source), the envelope pad with the margin and cap the dashed envelope
carries, n_peak, F_peak, on a line of its own at which offload the profile was
sized (`_sized_at`: x* in tonnes, x = 0 for a no_offload end; for a payload case "at the full
load with payload P_1* ... (dm_1; the run then flew P_2* ...)", since the drawn profile and
bars are dm_1, sized at P_1*, consistent with the payload table's "dm_1 (sized at P_1*)" row,
or that its P_2* search failed; the caption's longest line, which had run past the
figure's right edge when joined to the envelope line), dm by stage, the governing
element with its mode and dm (`_governing_text`: a relation element such as the thrust
structure or the interstage has no station profile, so the caption is the one place the figure
names it, and no annotation is drawn), whether stage 2 was sized and, for a
plausibility-scaled case, that the thickness profile is the unscaled sizing while the bars and
dm carry the factor; and says the profile is the model's sizing, not a measurement. Each
caption line is wrapped at `STRUCTURE_CAPTION_WRAP_CHARS` = 150 (about 174 characters reach
the right edge at the caption's 7 pt on the 9-in figure) with `STRUCTURE_CAPTION_INDENT` on
a continuation, and the rectangle tight_layout lays the panels in starts
`STRUCTURE_CAPTION_GAP` above the caption's measured top (`_layout_rect`), so a longer
caption (a payload case, a scaled case, a wrapped line) pushes the panels up instead of
running under the dm panel's axis label. Every
layout number of the figure is a named module constant (plots.py, the structure figure
section). A visual reviewer checks the bars against `structure_elements`, the annotation
against `structure_governing`, the labels against the drawn lines and the caption against
the record's keys.

**The console** (`cli.offload_lines`): one line per payload case after the pad controls
(status, P*, P* - P_ref, dm_1, c, the flag's name when it fired, and that the flight check
is not applicable to it).

**Three ways, from the record.** Every sentence that says what structural mass a run
charges for the push branches on the run's own record (the run-level keys of D-SP7-22,
"Coupling the structure to the offload solve", Records; on a recorded run its
`offload.runs` metrics record carries them, on a case, a structure payload case and a
sensitivity arm its record does; a sweep point writes no case record and no run
directory, so its structural solve is worded by the sweep summary's lines under its
table, `sweep_structure_lines` (fix round 2, H-S3a-P2-07) and, for a point whose case
ended no_offload, `sweep_no_offload_lines` (SP7 step S3c; its "carrying dm" clause for a
`structure_charged` record only), beside the sweep index's structure columns,
`offload_structure_index_values`, and its `<case>.dv_shortfall_mps` (the no_offload end's
shortfall on disk), and the Checks section, and the block caveat's sweep-point arm is reachable only by a synthetic record), never on the
experiment or on a global flag. The test is `summary.structure_charged` (`structure_charged` is True); a
penalty row is told by `replay.penalty_added_kg` as before; everything else is
uncharged. The uncharged branch keeps SP1's text word for word at every source, and the
penalty branch SP2's at every source but the exploratory banner, so every page and frame
of a directory without a structural record is unchanged (the gallery's five replay pages
regenerate byte for byte; the scene page differs only where the template changed: the CSP
script hash line, the data block's `version` key and the Data line of KI-038, and since
fix round 1 the run selector's group for structure payload cases; the phase file's
section 12 records the four regions). A new summary of
such a directory does change in four places: the comparison basis line (KI-039 and the
two dry-mass exceptions), the imposed cases' sub-section (KI-039, with the not-run list's
lead line and the energy note's both-tables sentence before it), the exploratory banner
of a directory with an imposed stage-1 case, which no longer prints the imposed-not-saved
sentence (D-SP2-27; the not-netted sentence of D-SP2-07 kept; "KI-039" below) and, for a
penalty row, the exploratory banner's push caveat, which names the row's assumed stage-1
dry mass (fix round 1, H-S3a-05; a deviation from step item 1's "keeps today's text",
logged in the phase file's section 12, since the bare "no structural mass for the push"
was false beside a penalty row); a directory
written outside a repository now reads "state unknown" on the scene page (fix round 2,
N2-04). The modelled branch's core sentence is one function,
`summary.modelled_structure_text(record, structure_inputs)`:

- the mass by stage: `<dm1 + dm2> kg (stage 1 <dm1> kg, stage 2 <dm2> kg)` from
  `structure_dm_kg` and `structure_dm_stage2_kg` (`modelled_mass_split_text`; a solve
  that found no x* has no dm and reads `no sizing at x* (the solve found no x*)`);
- the model, `STRUCTURE_MODEL_NAME` ("a first-order station sizing of the push load"),
  with the layer and set (`structure_layer_label`, "Reporting the structure") and the
  file (`structure_file`);
- the physics band's ends where the block's `structure_inputs` record them
  (`structure_band_text` on `structure_band_ends`: the frozen physics sets' polish of the
  headline search, `structure.SEARCH_HEADLINE`, its `dm_after_kg`, at the structure
  file's headline push, the one the sets' `method` names, named in the clause from the
  record's own `structure_inputs.sets.method` (`structure_band_push`, the pattern
  `STRUCTURE_SETS_PUSH_PATTERN` on the sentence `sim.structure_search_method` writes;
  `structure_band_push_text`: the gate file's "silo_offload_2d's silo_cold at a stage-1
  offload of 41,263 kg, per its sets.method", the README-loads file's
  "silo_offload_2d_readme's silo_cold at a stage-1 offload of 36,006 kg, per its
  sets.method"; `STRUCTURE_BAND_PUSH_FALLBACK`, "the push its sets.method names", when
  the method names none; final clean-up, N3a-02: fix round 3's constant "SP1's silo_cold
  at its stage-1 offload" held for the gate file alone); then, in a clause of its own,
  `STRUCTURE_BAND_SCOPE_TEXT`, "both ends are sizing-only numbers from the frozen sets,
  not this run's band", and how the record itself is sized (`structure_band_sized_text`
  on its `structure_sizing`): `STRUCTURE_BAND_SIZED_FLOWN`, "the run is sized at its own
  push and offload", or, for a full-load sizing (a full-load-sizing row, every structure
  payload case, which config sizes at x = 0), `STRUCTURE_BAND_SIZED_FULL_LOAD`, "the run
  is sized at its own push on the full load (x = 0)" (final clean-up, N3a-01; fix round
  3, H-S3a-P3-05: the earlier "this run's band only if its push is that one" named a
  condition no reader could check and no coupled run meets); a file without frozen sets,
  or sets without a headline polish, gets no band clause, never a made-up end). D-SP7-41:
  when the block's `structure_inputs.plausibility` records a factor other than 1 on an
  end (`structure_band_factors`), that end is printed unscaled beside its value after the
  factor, with the rule's trigger (M_model / R and the element carrying the largest share
  of M_model in the pad envelope) inside that end's parenthesis ("dm 3,677 kg unscaled
  (2,717 kg after the plausibility rule's factor 0.739; the rule fires at M_model / R =
  1.76, ...) and 18,604 kg"; fix round 3, S3A-NUM-05: never after the other end), or
  after both ends "on both ends" when the rule scales both, on every record, scaled or
  not (fix round 2, H-S3a-P2-02); a scaled record of a block without that record says
  both ends are before the rule's factor (fix round 1, H-S3a-03). The factors are the
  rule's on the experiment's own pad envelope at the central coefficients;
- when the plausibility rule scaled the dm (`structure_plausibility_scaled`), its factor
  (`structure_plausibility_factor`, D-SP7-33);
- the run's own fired flags by name (`structure_flags_text`; `STRUCTURE_NO_FLAG_TEXT`
  when none fired; `STRUCTURE_FLAGS_NOT_SIZED` without a sizing at x*;
  `STRUCTURE_FLAGS_NOT_RECORDED_TEXT` for a record without a flag list, never read as
  clean: fix round 2, N2-06); beside a fired `structure_release_unload` whose stage-1
  column separates at the push (`release_flag_pressures`: a stage-1 bottom pressure below
  0 absolute), D-SP7-39's comparison from the flag's own numbers
  (`release_flag_comparison_text`, fix round 2, H-S3a-P2-01): the separation comes from
  the single-mode step treatment, which the pad's own MECO shutdown is put through too,
  with the full stage-2 LOX column's bottom gauge pressure there against the push's, and
  "so it separates on the pad as well and the separation is not specific to the push"
  when MECO's value is below 0, else "so on the pad it does not separate"; a flag fired
  for the dome or the upper stack alone adds nothing (its numbers and MECO's are in its
  flag line);
- `STRUCTURE_ESTIMATE_TEXT`: a first-order estimate with its stated ranges, not a
  detailed structural design.

It never calls the mass assumed and never calls the band "bounds". The sources:

- the summary's offload block caveats (`summary.offload_caveats`, written into the
  record's `caveats` by `results_io.planar_offload` from the block's structural records,
  cases, payload cases and arms alike, and from each case's and payload case's drive,

### The flown push of a linear motor (SP7 step S4b)

Modules: `src/launchsim/sim.py` (`flown_push_trace`, `linear_motor_push_load`,
`_flown_history`, `PUSH_SAMPLE_TAGS`, `PUSH_SAMPLE_N`, `PUSH_SAMPLE_F_INT`,
`PUSH_SAMPLE_BOUNDARY`, `PUSH_HISTORY_GAP_FRACTION`, `StructureTransform.push_context`,
`.flies_push` and `.push`,
`build_structure_transform`, `structure_push_assumptions`; `simulate` and `simulate_planar`
call `run_wide_felt_with_track_peak` on a linear-motor run), `src/launchsim/structure.py`
(`single_mode_bound`, `SingleModeBound`, `SINGLE_MODE_STEP_FRACTION`, `FlownHistory` and
`.bound_weights`, `FLOWN_PEAK_KINDS`, `FLOWN_BOUND_WEIGHTS`, `FLOWN_BOUND_REL_TOL`,
`PushLoad.history`; `ReleaseState.rise_plateau_g`, `taper_time_s`,
`taper_drop_g` and `.from_flown_push`; `PushRequirement.dlf_rise`, `n_bound_g`,
`f_bound_N`, `release_rise_plateau_g`, `release_rise_residual_g`, `release_taper_time_s`,
`release_taper_dlf`, `release_taper_residual_g`, `release_bound_residual_g` and
`release_compression_g`;
`push_requirement`, `_flown_case_peaks`, `_release_flag`, `FLOWN_RELEASE_FLAG_KEYS`,
`FLOWN_PUSH_FLAG_KEYS`, `FLOWN_PUSH_RELEASE_COMPRESSION_KEY`), `src/launchsim/metrics.py`
(`track_scan`, `TrackScan`,
`track_peaks`, `TrackPeak`, `track_felt_and_interface`, `FELT_AND_INTERFACE_COUNT`,
`TRACK_PEAK_SCAN_POINTS`, `TRACK_PEAK_XATOL_S`, `TRACK_PEAK_TIE_REL`, `linear_motor_track_peaks`,
`LINEAR_MOTOR_EXACT_PEAK_METRICS`, `run_wide_felt_with_track_peak`; `track_metrics`),
`src/launchsim/metrics_planar.py` (`planar_track_metrics`), `src/launchsim/config.py`
(`_refuse_unused_rise_time`), `src/launchsim/summary.py` (`STRUCTURE_FLOWN_PUSH_NOTE`,
`structure_push_is_flown`) and `src/launchsim/results_io.py` (the flown push's assumption
line). Tests: `tests/test_structure_linear_motor.py` and, on fake runs,
`tests/test_structure_pipeline.py::test_a_linear_motor_structural_case_flies_its_push_in_the_pass`,
`::test_a_linear_motor_structure_payload_case_flies_its_push_at_full_load` and
`::test_a_rise_time_override_on_a_linear_motor_structural_case_is_refused`. Design 4.2.1,
4.2.2 and 4.4 (D-SP7-16, D-SP7-20), the S4b row of section 5 and exit criterion 6; KI-046.
Review round 1 of S4b (M1, M2, H-P1-02) found the rise formula alone unconservative on
flown pushes; the flown history's bound below is its fix, and review round 2 (P2-M1) its
step floor for the planner's ultra-short sub-phases.

**The flight.** A structural case whose variant's drive is `linear_motor` flies its push
inside the transform. `build_structure_transform` keeps the start run's `SearchContext`
(`search_context` of its `planar_setup`: the context `offload_problem_factory` gives the
solve, built anew, so a copy) as `push_context`, and every sizing of the fixed point flies,
with `flown_push_trace`, that context's planner for the vehicle at x carrying the iterate
dm, at the payload it flies, in FINAL_MODE (the final tolerance; rtol 1e-10 in the shipped
budget) with dense output, through `PlanarPlanner.start` only: the hold of a start lit
before the push, the push and the release (the track end, or the release speed's root,
S4a), no ascent (design 4.4: `ctx.planner(P_ref, final).start(assist, track)`). Nothing
tightens the push automatically: a caller that tightens the solve (`SearchContext.tightened`)
passes the same tightened context as the transform's `push_context`
(`dataclasses.replace`), as the convergence test does. A push that does not release
(`drive_stall`, `drive_limit`) raises `search.PreludeFailure` with the planner's status: an
offload evaluation that meets it is infeasible (also where only an iterate fails: a dm = 0
first iterate can stall near an acceleration law's drive_limit threshold although the
vehicle carrying the converged dm would fly; "Stays out" below). The builder flies
the sizing at x = 0 once (the full-load stack at P_ref, from dm = 0 through its fixed
point's iterates, where the solve and the record start) and refuses a case whose push
fails to release at one of those iterates (the first that fails ends the build) with a
ValueError naming the status, before the
case's solve (review round 1, m1; round 2, H-P2-06): the experiment still ends with
FAILED.txt, now with this message before the solve instead of a PreludeFailure from the
offload pass's sizings at 0 after it. Measured on the development machine in a short burst
(the force law over 50 m, six iterates per sizing): one flight about 16 ms, its reduction
(scan, exact maxima and history) about 6 ms, the history's two bounds about 0.5 ms per
`push_requirement` call (up to 1 ms in review round 2's measurement) and the increment
about 4 ms, so a transform call (one sizing of six iterates) about 0.15 s (constant_accel's
analytic call: 21 to 76 ms); under sustained load the machine throttles and the same call
takes about 0.38 s. The slow coupled solve below spent 33 s with its verification,
unthrottled.

**The governing samples** (`linear_motor_push_load`; design 4.4: "maximum n, maximum F_int,
maximum head per tank, the events"). Every PUSH load case is a flown state, with n = (F_int
+ T)/(m_v g0), its interface force and thrust, and the tank contents at that instant (the
stage-1 propellant m_v - m_fixed, m_fixed the stage-1 dry mass, stage 2 wet, the fairing and
the payload, split by the LOX fraction; stage 2 full), at:

- the exact maxima over the push of n, F_int, n m_v (= (F_int + T)/g0, the thrust-structure
  entry's load) and n m_prop1 (the head at each stage-1 barrel's bottom, p - p_u = n g0
  m/A: both tanks keep the mixture fraction, so one instant serves both; stage 2's contents
  do not change on the track, so its heads peak with n);
- every sub-phase start: the push start, the drive's kinks and watch crossings
  (`drive_ramp_end`, `power_limit`, `drive_cap`, their ends, `taper_start`), the thrust
  kinks, the thrust clamp and an ignition on the track: the events;

one case per instant, labelled with every sample there (`PUSH_SAMPLE_TAGS`, "max <kind>"
in `FLOWN_PEAK_KINDS`' order, the logged event names or `PUSH_SAMPLE_BOUNDARY`); an instant
is one float time, so maxima refined by separate searches can land a few ulps apart as
separate cases (the four maxima of the Airy push below within 3.1e-15 s), and the starts of
the planner's ultra-short sub-phases each give a case (two `taper_start` cases 3e-15 s
apart there; review round 4, H-P4-01). The resting
values are those at push start, n_0 = g_eff sin phi(0)/g0 and F_0 = m_v(0) g_eff sin phi(0)
- T(0): cold, the vehicle's weight component on the carriage; hot, the hold's (the thrust on
the clamped vehicle); the forms of constant_accel's case. A trace whose push-start mass is
not the vehicle's liftoff mass less the hold's burn (within `STRUCTURE_MASS_TOL_KG`) is
refused. The PushLoad also carries the push's load history (`FlownHistory`, the input of
the bound below): n, F_int, the vehicle mass and the stage-1 propellant on the dense scan of
every sub-phase (`metrics.track_scan`'s 256 samples, the sub-phase's own start and end
states at its ends, each case's instant inserted with its own values and the scan samples
within a quarter spacing of it removed, `PUSH_HISTORY_GAP_FRACTION`; cases a few ulps apart
stay separate entries, history intervals down to 4.4e-16 s on the Airy push, which
`SINGLE_MODE_STEP_FRACTION` below reads as steps), a sub-phase boundary appearing twice,
with each case's grid entry and the maxima it is the case of.

The reduction's limit: a station driver that mixes n and the contents, n (m + c), is read
at the cases only: a head above a barrel's bottom (c < 0), the aft and common domes sized at
their crowns and the transfer tube at its bottom (c = rho A b or rho A (L_tube + b) > 0,
`_dome_driver_offset`), a barrel's compression with the column above it (the RP-1 barrel's
with the LOX column, c > 0); so is the thrust-structure entry's load F_peak + T, which mixes
F_int and F_int + T when its factor exceeds 1 (with constant thrust it peaks with F_int). On
a cold push the contents are constant and every driver peaks with n. On a force plateau
with constant thrust n (m + c) = (F + T_sys)(m + c)/(M g0) is a ratio of two linear
functions of t, so monotone between the samples. Measured on two hot pushes (a force plateau
with a 20 t carriage and f_imp 0.5; a push lit 0.3 s after its start whose corner at 15 m/s
puts it in its power phase), over 30 values of c from -0.9 to 2 times the stage-1
propellant (a range that covers the domes' and the tube's offsets), the cases' maximum (the
release case, which the sizing does not read, left out) equals the dense maximum to
rounding (gap 0.0).

**Exact maxima** (`metrics.track_peaks`; KI-046). The pattern of
`losses.drive_power_extrema` and `metrics_planar.scan_peak` on the ASSIST sub-phases: each
sub-phase's own start and end states are candidates (a peak on a boundary is exact: the
drive's kinks, the thrust kinks, the watch crossings, the release); inside a sub-phase each
quantity is evaluated at `TRACK_PEAK_SCAN_POINTS` = 256 samples of one vectorised
dense-output evaluation (`track_scan`, whose scan the history reuses), and every sample at
least as high as its neighbours and strictly higher than one of them brackets a local
maximum that a bounded Brent search refines to `TRACK_PEAK_XATOL_S` = 1e-10 s. Every kink of
the linear motor's force is a sub-phase boundary (D-SP7-49; KI-048's exceptions aside), so
each quantity is smooth inside a sub-phase and a maximum is missed only when two lie within
one scan spacing.

A flat maximum keeps its earliest instant (review round 3, P3-M1). The candidates are
offered in time order (a sub-phase's start, its interior, its end), and one replaces the
incumbent only when it exceeds it by more than `TRACK_PEAK_TIE_REL` = 1e-12 relative; a
sample above both neighbours by no more than that is not refined (on a smooth quantity a
refine gains at most a quarter of its excess). The value kept is within 1.25e-12 relative of
the largest. Without the rule rounding chose the instant: on a force plateau without a
carriage M = m_v, so F_int = F_max and n m_v = (F_max + T)/g0 are flat from the end of the
rise to the release, and on a hot push the contents change along that plateau (n rises
from 5.2228 to 5.2539 g0 on the hot 50 m push). The max-F_int and max-n m_v cases wandered
from 0.500 to 0.577 s as dm changed by 0.2 kg, each charged its own n, contents and grid
entry, so the increment S(dm), governed by the stage-1 RP-1 barrel's mixed driver, jumped by
-0.41 to +0.53 kg between dm 0.2 kg apart: every sizing of that push hit the fixed point's cap of 25
(contraction 36 to 87), and dm(x) was noise (10 g slopes of -29 and -44 kg/kg against 1 kg
slopes of +0.15 and -0.39). With the rule those cases sit at t_r with the `drive_ramp_end`
event at every dm, the history grid keeps one size, and the brackets on the flat plateau
are no longer refined (on that push about 200 Brent searches per reduction; measured in one
burst with the structure file read once, a reduction takes 112 to 119 ms with the tie set
to 0 against 8.0 to 8.4 ms with it, the flight about 20 ms; review round 4, C-P4-01 and
H-P4-02: round 3's 0.4 and 0.09 s included a read of the structure file, about 45 ms, in
each call). On a cold push the instant was harmless (n, the masses and
the contents are constant on the plateau), and the tie moves the cold max-n case to t_r
with every number unchanged to rounding. The same rule places the run metrics'
`felt_g_track_peak_t_s` and `_mass_kg` at a flat plateau's earliest instant instead of
where rounding puts them (a hot acceleration law's n).

Against a closed form (KI-046): a cold force-law push from the holding force with
F_max = M (3 g0 + g), t_r 4 s and a 90 m stop taper on a 100 m stroke enters its taper about
2 s into its rise (s = j t^3/6 with j = 3 g0/t_r up to L - s_t). On the taper inside the
rise x = L - s obeys

    x'' = -(j t/s_t) x,   x = alpha Ai(-k t) + beta Bi(-k t),   k = (j/s_t)^(1/3)

(Airy's equation; alpha and beta from x = s_t and x' = -j t_1^2/2 at the taper's start
t_1), so n = (g + j t x/s_t)/g0 and F_int = M (g + j t x/s_t) peak at the root of x + t x' =
0, inside the sub-phase (t* = 2.7613 s, n* = 2.7093 g0 on the planar track).
`track_peaks` matches the Airy peak to rounding (0 and 2.2e-16 relative, planar and 1-D;
its time within 3.7e-8 s). The same helper makes two run metrics exact on a linear-motor
push that did not stall (`linear_motor_track_peaks`, `LINEAR_MOTOR_EXACT_PEAK_METRICS`):
`felt_g_track_peak` with its time and mass, and `interface_force_peak_N` with its alias
`peak_interface_force_N`, 1-D and planar, keys and order unchanged; on that push the
sampled rows' maxima are 1.98e-5 relative below them (KI-046's 2e-5). After the merge
`run_wide_felt_with_track_peak` lifts the run-wide `peak_felt_axial_g` (time, mass, phase
ASSIST) to the exact track peak when it exceeds the run-wide value (the sampled rows', with
the flight's scan peak on a planar run), so the run-wide peak is never below the track's.
constant_accel's metrics stay the sampled rows' (exact for its monotone forces: the 1-D
golden tier and the planar output capture are unchanged); the minima, `drive_force_peak_N`
and the track-normal peaks stay sampled.

**The dynamic factor: the rise formula and the flown history's bound** (`push_requirement`,
`single_mode_bound`; design 4.2.1, D-SP7-16; review round 1, M1 and M2). The linear motor's
PushLoad states `rise_time_s` = the drive's `force_rise_time_s` and no RampedPlateau, so
under `rise_time` the rise formula takes DLF_rise = min(2, 1 + T/(pi t_r)) with the drive's
t_r (2 at t_r = 0, a step) and T = 1/f the coefficient set's axial period; no plateau raise
is charged, since the rise is flown (its cost is in the trajectory: `structure_ramp_cost_rel`
is null). The structure file's assumed real-drive rise time (`dynamics.rise_time_s`), which
exists because constant_accel flies a step, does not act on a linear-motor case: neither
the central value, nor a set's, nor a case override (refused when the experiment is
resolved, `config._refuse_unused_rise_time`: "vary force_rise_time_s instead"; review round
1, C-P1-02). The formula n_0 + DLF_rise (n - n_0) is the single mode's worst-phase peak
only for a load that ramps linearly from rest over t_r to a plateau. A flown load does not
always: a hot push whose delivered thrust exceeds the stack's weight (the default carriage
0 t and f_imp 0: the drive's force at push start is 0) steps at clamp release (n from
0.9965 to 1.3617 g0 on the gate vehicle at P_ref, F_int from F_0 = m_v g - T = -2.04 MN to
0); an acceleration law capped by F_max, a power corner or a
taper reaches its largest value before t_r; a power corner, a taper and a release cut the
load's slope. Review round 1 measured the formula up to 3.9% (n) and 5.3% (F_int) below the
single mode's response on such pushes at 3 and 5 Hz. Every flown push therefore takes,
beside the formula, the phase-free single-mode bound of its flown history.

The flown load q(t) (n or F_int) is taken as the piecewise-linear interpolant of its history
from rest at q_0 (n_0 or F_0, zero slope). The single mode x'' = -w^2 (x - q), w = 2 pi/T,
from rest responds exactly as

    x = q - sum_k [J_k cos(w tau_k) + D_k sin(w tau_k)/w]

with J_k the load's steps (the first entry's jump from q_0 among them), D_k its slope jumps
(from zero slope at rest) and tau_k = t - t_k. Each term is bounded on its own, whatever its
phase relative to the others (none of their cancellations is credited, nor damping), from
what its own elapsed time fixes: |J cos| <= |J|; a slope decrease (D < 0) gives |D|
sin(u)/w <= |D| min(tau, 1/w); a slope increase (D > 0) gives -D sin(u)/w, at most 0 for its
first half period (the mode lags a rising slope) and D min(1/w, tau - T/2) after it. So

    x - q <= rho(t) = min(V(t), sum |J_k| + sum |D_k| min(1/w, max(0, t - t_k*)))

with t_k* = t_k for a slope decrease and t_k + T/2 for an increase, and V the load's total
variation from q_0 (the step bound: |z| <= V for z = (x - q) + i x'/w, whose rate is -i w z
- q'). On a ramp from rest to a plateau rho reaches min(Delta, 2 r/w) = (DLF_rise - 1) Delta
once the plateau has lasted: the formula, which the bound reproduces to rounding on every
flown push whose n and F_int ramp linearly from rest to a plateau that outlasts that
saturation (the cold force law, a cold stop taper after the rise included, whose fall only
lowers q + rho; the acceleration law's n; measured equal within 1e-11). A step J at push
start adds J; a load that peaks at t' < t_r is charged the ramp it flew, (DLF(t') - 1)
Delta. A slope change contributes nothing at its own instant, and a slope increase nothing
for its first half period. A slope decrease on a load that is not rising (a corner off a
plateau) raises rho no faster than q falls, so it never raises q + rho; inside a rise (old
slope r > 0, new slope -s) its term (r + s) min(tau, 1/w) outgrows the fall, so q + rho
keeps rising at r for up to 1/w after the corner (review round 2, H-P2-02). Between
consecutive breakpoints (the entries, t_k* and t_k* + 1/w) q, V and S = sum |J| + the slope
terms are linear and rho = min(V, S) piecewise linear: q + V rises at q' + |q'| >= 0, and
where q + S falls q' < 0 (S never falls), so q + V is flat there; q + rho = min(q + V, q +
S) therefore peaks on a breakpoint, and its maximum over the push is exact for the PL
model. Under `step` rho = V (every change charged as a step: the peak is the load plus its
total variation from rest, n + V), under `quasi_static` 0 (the bound is skipped there: it
is the load itself).

Rest at push start is exact for n and a premise for F_int on a hot push (review round 4,
P4-m1). On the clamp n stays g_eff sin phi/g0 whatever the thrust, so n's mode is at rest
there. F_int = m_v g_eff sin phi - T(t) is not constant on the clamp: the startup ramp
lowers it by about the thrust (from 5.59 to -2.04 MN on the gate vehicle at P_ref, the
tests' start lit 2 s before its push), and under a start whose ramp ends at push start it
is still changing at that instant. The bound, the formula's F_0 and the tests' oracle all
take F_0 as rest, so that change is no forcing of F_int's mode. The justification: the
thrust and the clamp both react at the stack's aft end, so on the clamp the change moves
load between two forces at that end and leaves the load the stack above carries, n m_v g0,
unchanged; design 4.2.1 prescribes the hold's value as F_0, and constant_accel's hot F_0
carries the same convention. The convention is not uniform: the same thrust ramp flown on
the track (lit after push start, with a carriage) is charged as a forcing of F_int's mode.
Measured (review round 4: a single mode of F_int driven from rest at m_v g_eff at ignition by
the hold's own F_int, the HoldParams schedule with its back-pressure clamp, then by the
flown push): on a hot force-law push with a 20 t carriage and f_imp 0.5, over 2 to 10 Hz
in 0.25 Hz steps and t_r 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 and 1.0 s, that oracle exceeds the charged F_peak
in 32 of the 132 configurations, by up to 0.456 MN (2.3%; 2.5 Hz, t_r 1.0 s; 0.454 MN at
t_r 0.6 s), 0.372 MN (1.95%) at 3.5 Hz with t_r 1.0 s and 0.302 MN (1.5%) at 3 Hz with t_r
0.8 s; on a hot acceleration law with a 250 t carriage by 0.185 MN (0.8%) at 1.25 Hz,
outside the band. The hold leaves F_int's mode a free oscillation of at most 0.533 MN in
the band (2 Hz; 0.487 at 2.5 Hz), which raises the oracle's maximum by at most that much,
so the hot pushes without a carriage (a step at clamp release), whose charged F_peak lies
1.2 to 4.0 MN above the oracle from rest at the seven frequencies measured from 2.5 to 5
Hz, stay covered there, and no test sees the excess. n is unaffected. "Stays out" below
lists it.

The PL model is the history's grid, with two limits. First, a grid interval no longer than
`SINGLE_MODE_STEP_FRACTION` = 1e-6 of the period is a step: its change enters J and V,
never a slope (review round 2, P2-M1). The planner leaves ASSIST sub-phases of 3e-15 to
1e-10 s at a stop taper's `taper_start` and at a `power_limit` corner (event location),
and the scan puts 256 samples on each, so their differences are rounding: read as slopes
(up to +-16 g0/s at one ulp of time) and each charged at min(tau, 1/w), they had lifted the
cold 50 m push with a 10 m taper from the formula's 4.540 to 6.346 g0 (F_peak +40%) and left
its transform's fixed point at the cap of 25, dm jumping by tonnes per kilogram of offload.
The mode cannot tell a change over w dt <= 2 pi x 1e-6 from a step (a step's |J| covers a
short ramp's amplitude |Delta| |sin(w dt/2)|/(w dt/2)), so the rule costs nothing physical;
a whole sub-phase shorter than about 255 x 1e-6 T (85 us at 3 Hz) is then one step of its
change, at most its slope times that span. Second, the slope content near a corner depends
on the grid's spacing there (`metrics.TRACK_PEAK_SCAN_POINTS` per sub-phase; review round
2, P2-m1): a corner in a short sub-phase is resolved at once, one at the start of a long
sub-phase over its first spacing, its curvature spread over the next samples. Both are
valid bounds of their PL models (the models' interpolation error is about 0.01 g0 there,
review round 2's estimate), but they differ: on a cold 60 m push whose power corner sits at
the ramp-end speed v_r (1 + eps), the corner 0.18 ms before t_r (eps = -1e-3, resolved at
once) charges n_peak 4.7529 g0 against 4.6927 g0 at eps = +-1e-5 (resolved over the 12 ms
first spacing of the following 3 s sub-phase): +0.060 g0, F_peak +1.3%, the release bound
+0.12 g0. The vehicle's mass moves the corner's time with x and dm, so dm(x) can step by
about 1% of the push's load where a corner crosses such a boundary (not measured on a
solve).

Each case is charged the larger of the formula and the bound (`_flown_case_peaks`): n_peak
= max(n_0 + DLF_rise (n - n_0), n + rho_n at the case's instant), F_peak likewise with F_0
and rho_F; the case of the largest n is raised to the bound's maximum of n + rho_n over the
push (`n_bound_g`), the case of the largest F_int to that of F_int (`f_bound_N`), and the
cases of the largest n m_v and n m_prop1 so that their n m is the bound's largest (n +
rho_n) m over the push. The bound replaces the formula's value only where it exceeds it by
more than `FLOWN_BOUND_REL_TOL` = 1e-10 relative (their rounding apart on a linear ramp:
the grid slopes' rounding only adds to sum |D_k|, and on 60 cold pushes the bound lay
+2.7e-13 to +7.9e-13 above the formula, too close to the earlier 1e-12; review round 3,
P3-m1). The
requirement's dlf is the factor the charged n_peak carries, (n_peak - n_0)/(n_q - n_0), the
formula's where the formula governs, so the summary's row n_peak = n_rest + DLF (n_q -
n_rest) holds; `dlf_rise` keeps the formula's. The heads use n_peak. Against the single-mode
oracle (x'' = -w^2 (x - q(t)) integrated on the flown dense output from rest at push
start, the premise above, DOP853 at rtol 1e-10; it reproduces the ramp's exact peak where |sin(pi t_r/T)| = 1 to 1e-7), on the
eleven configurations of review round 1 and the release in tension of review round 3 (at 3
and 5 Hz; "The release" below) the charged n_peak and F_peak are at least its maxima, the
release swing at most the lowest load it keeps after the release and the compression after
the release at least the largest (`test_the_charged_push_bounds_the_single_mode_oracle`).
Measured margins (charged less oracle, re-measured after the step floor, which removed
rounding from four of the eleven): n_peak 0.0022 to 0.749 g0 and F_peak 0.046% to 20.4%
(relative to |F|; the release in tension's interface force is negative throughout).
The hot push with a step at clamp release at t_r 0.5 s, 5 Hz, charges n_peak 6.204 against
the oracle's 5.954 g0 (the formula 5.888) and F_peak 5.4% above the oracle's; the
acceleration law capped in a 0.5 s rise at 5 Hz 0.020 g0; the taper entered in the rise at
5 Hz 0.030 g0 (0.157 before the floor); a lm_fixed_r07-like push (F_max 24 MN, P_max 0.7
F_max x 77 m/s, release at L) 0.0022 g0 at 5 Hz and 0.0063 g0 at 3 Hz above the formula,
which there equals the oracle. The bound is conservative by its construction: the
phase-free sum (a hot push's step and ramp at their worst common phase), a corner inside a
rise (q + rho rising at the old slope for 1/w after it), and the first-order count of a
curving load, which charges the power phase's relaxing slope at worst phase after its
first half period and does not credit the lag the mode keeps on a curving q (the 0.0022
and 0.0063 g0 above). The extreme case, a 5 m/s corner inside a 0.5 s rise at 3 Hz,
charges n_peak 4.422 against the formula's 4.103 and the oracle's 3.673 g0 (4.478 before
the floor): of its 0.320 g0 over the formula about 0.077 comes from the corner itself (the
same history with a straight fall at the first spacing's slope after the corner gives
4.179) and 0.243 from the curvature of the power phase after it. On the hot carriage push
(the mass burns, so n and F_int curve) the bound exceeds the formula by 1.5e-5 relative on
F_peak.

**The release** (`ReleaseState`, `push_requirement`, `_release_flag`; design 4.2.2). The
release state is the flown one: n_before the felt load at the release instant (the track
end, or the release speed's root before it, S4a), n_after = T(t_rel)/(m_v g0) (drag
neglected, as constant_accel's), the contents then; the facility length is S4a's
(`linear_motor_facility_m`). constant_accel holds its plateau to the release (n_before =
n_q), so its release peak n_0 + DLF (n_q - n_0) carries the rise's undamped residual (DLF -
1)(n_q - n_0). A flown push's load at the release can lie below its largest (a power phase,
the release at a target speed in it or at the track end after a corner, or a stop taper; a
release at a target speed inside the rise does not: the load rises through the rise, so
there n_before = n_q), so its release state names the push's largest flown quasi-static
load n_q (`rise_plateau_g`), and

    n_peak,rel = n_before + A,  A = max((DLF_rise - 1)(n_q - n_0) [+ (DLF_taper - 1) drop_taper], A_rel)
    n_swing    = n_after - |n_before - n_after| - A
    n_comp     = n_after + |n_before - n_after| + A

the rise formula's residual taken from n_q, which the load at the rise's end does not
exceed. A bounds the amplitude |z| about n_before just before the release, z = (x -
n_before) + i x'/w; the drop to n_after moves the load, not the mode, so about n_after z' =
(x - n_after) + i x'/w = (n_before - n_after) + z and the mode keeps at most |n_before -
n_after| + A:
n_swing is the lowest load after the release (`release_swing_g`) and n_comp the largest
(`release_compression_g`; review round 3, H-P3-01). A release that unloads the stack
(n_after <= n_before) gives the forms of S2, n_swing = 2 n_after - n_peak,rel and n_comp =
n_peak,rel. A release in tension (F_int < 0 at the release, so n_after = T/(m_v g0) exceeds
n_before; S4's "Linear motor" flags it `interface_tensile`) loads the stack instead: n_swing
= n_before - A and n_comp = 2 n_after - n_before + A, above n_peak,rel. A hot force law at
6 MN on a 250 t carriage with f_imp 0.5 over 30 m releases with F_int = -0.85 MN, n_before
1.242 and n_after 1.397 g0: at 3 Hz n_peak,rel 1.294, n_comp 1.605 and n_swing 1.190
against the oracle's post-release 1.597 and 1.198 (0.008 g0 margins; at 5 Hz 0.035);
S2's forms had given a compression of 1.294 and a swing of 1.501. n_comp is checked only
by the payload-limit flag, never sized: the stations are sized at n_peak (the heads above).
In tension the oracle's own maximum after the release lies well above n_peak (review round
4, P4-m2; at 3 Hz): 1.597 against 1.294 g0 on this push, 1.812 against 1.281 with a 6 m/s
power corner (n_before 1.025) and 1.830 against 1.290 g0 (42% above) with an 8 m stop
taper, which ends near the holding force (n_before 0.9965, n_after 1.3975). Such a release
repeats the pad's own hold-down release, n stepping from about 1.0 to T/(m g0), about 1.4
g0, with full tanks; the pad's quasi-static envelope (its flown rows) does not carry that
step's overshoot either, so leaving it out keeps the increment consistent with the pad
("Stays out" below). Nor is the interface's tension sized (review round 4, H-P4-05): S4's
`interface_tensile` (the vehicle would have to be held back on the carriage) charges no
hold-back hardware, and the load ring is sized for the largest interface force F_peak alone,
0 kg when F_peak <= 0. On this push F_int stays negative throughout (-2.04 MN at rest,
-0.80 MN at t_r, the charged F_peak -0.535 MN), so it charges no ring, against 605 kg for
the cold 50 m push of the tests; the claims on F_int here, the bound's and the oracle's,
cover its largest value, not its most negative. The swing with every
residual damped (`release_swing_plateau_g`) is n_after - |n_before - n_after|: 2 n_after -
n_before, or n_before in tension. constant_accel's release keeps S2's forms, which carry
the same premise that the release unloads (n_after <= n_before; its `push_requirement`
path is unchanged, "Stays out" below). With a stop taper (design 4.2.2: "for a taper, its own ramp DLF") the formula adds a
ramp down of drop_taper = (the largest n from its start on) - n_before over t_taper = t_rel -
t_start, measured from the taper's start (its `taper_start` event, or the push start for a
taper active from s = 0), not from the load's peak: a taper entered in the rise first lets
the load rise (the Airy push falls from its peak for 1.86 s of its 2.61 s); DLF_taper =
`dynamic_load_factor`(t_taper, T, mode). A_rel is the bound's amplitude at the release
(`release_bound_residual_g`): with the slope cut there, the oscillation's amplitude about
the load just before the drop, q(t_rel) = n_before, is |z| of z = sum_k [-J_k e^{-i u_k} + i
D_k (1 - e^{-i u_k})/w] (review round 3, H-P3-01: not about n_after), so

    A_rel = min(V, sum |J| + (sum |D| + |q'(t_rel)|)/w, sum |J| + sum |D| min(tau, 2/w))

under `rise_time` (no sign credited: an amplitude), V under `step` (the fall n_q - n_before
included) and 0 under `quasi_static`. A release that cuts a ramp keeps r min(t, 2/w), where
the formula gave (DLF_rise - 1) r t; a power corner adds its slope change and the release its
cut (review round 1, M2 and H-P1-02: the power phase's fall is not slow on this measure,
since a corner's residual is |dq/dt jump|/w whatever the fall's length). A cold force-law
taper ends at the holding force, so there n_before = n_0: a 40 m taper after a 0.5 s rise
over a 100 m stroke takes 0.6198 s (atan(s_t Omega/v_0)/Omega, Omega = sqrt(a_f/s_t)),
DLF_taper 1.1712 at 3 Hz; the formula's swing is -2.117 g0 (residuals 0.620 + 0.500), but
the bound governs there (A_rel 1.144 g0) and the charged swing is -2.141 g0, against -0.996
with every residual damped (2 n_after - n_before; the same push released at the track end
without a taper: -4.540, charged). A force-law push released at 40 m/s in its power phase
from a 30 m/s corner has n_before 2.940 below n_q 3.920, and there the bound governs. The
release flag records how its peak was built (`FLOWN_RELEASE_FLAG_KEYS`: `release_rise_plateau_g`,
`release_rise_residual_g`, with a taper `release_taper_time_s`, `release_taper_dlf`,
`release_taper_residual_g`, and `release_bound_residual_g`, after `meco_swing_g`) and the
payload-limit flag the push's (`FLOWN_PUSH_FLAG_KEYS`: `dlf_rise`, `n_bound_g`, `f_bound_N`,
after its limits, then `release_compression_g`, `FLOWN_PUSH_RELEASE_COMPRESSION_KEY`). That
flag also checks n_comp against the upper axial limit beside n_peak (review rounds 2 and 3,
P2-m2 and H-P3-01): the phase-free release bound can lift n_comp = n_peak,rel above n_peak
on a release that unloads (on the configurations above 4.084 against 3.882 g0 past a 10 m/s
corner at 3 Hz, 2.709 against 2.320 for a 1 m/s release inside the rise; the oracle's
post-release maxima stayed below n_peak on all fourteen such configurations measured, the
closest 2.849 against 2.868 g0, a 2 m/s release inside the rise), and a release in tension
lifts n_comp above both (1.605 against n_peak and n_peak,rel of 1.294 g0 above, and the
oracle's 1.597). constant_accel's flag values stay S2's
lists and its check S2's (its plateau holds to the release, so n_peak,rel = n_peak), and its
`push_requirement` path is unchanged bit for bit. Measured against the oracle the release
bound is the most conservative part (phase-free over the rise, the corner and the cut): on
the eleven configurations of review round 1 the charged swing lies 0.11 to 1.81 g0 beyond
the oracle's at the check's frequency (1.9 before the step floor), and n_comp as far above
its post-release maximum; on the release in tension, whose bound is small (A 0.052 g0 at 3
Hz), 0.008 and 0.035 g0 at 3 and 5 Hz.

**The fixed point on a flown push.** As S3's: each call starts from dm = 0 and iterates
dm_{k+1} = S(push(m(x) + dm_k)) to `STRUCTURE_FIXED_POINT_TOL_KG` = 1e-6 kg under the cap of
25 with its flag; the push is flown afresh for each iterate (under the cold force law n =
F_max/(M g0) falls as dm grows while F_int = F_max stays; under the acceleration law F_int
grows with it). Measured on the synthetic file and pad, the force law over 50 m (F_max 22 MN,
t_r 0.5 s): six sizings per call (steps 5,966, 63.0, 0.66, 6.8e-3, 7.1e-5 and 7.4e-7 kg at x
= 20 t), contraction 0.0103 to 0.0106 from x = 0 to 40 t (the acceleration law at a_cmd 3
g0, flying its command at 20 and 40 t: 0.0047 and 0.0048), recorded in the cap flag as S3
